items.title: Alaska ends deal to give voter records to US Justice Department
items.summary:
Alaska ends deal to give voter records to US Justice Department
The decision follows the conclusion of the 2026 midterm elections and an effort under Trump to collect state voter rolls.
Alaska has terminated a memorandum of understanding that granted the United States Department of Justice (DOJ) acc
items.text:
Alaska ends deal to give voter records to US Justice Department
The decision follows the conclusion of the 2026 midterm elections and an effort under Trump to collect state voter rolls.
Alaska has terminated a memorandum of understanding that granted the United States Department of Justice (DOJ) access to the state’s voter rolls.
On Monday, outgoing Lieutenant Governor Nancy Dahlstrom, who oversees the state’s elections, announced she had notified the Justice Department that Alaska was withdrawing from the 2025 memo, effective immediately.
In a statement, Dahlstrom said her state had entered the agreement “in good faith to cooperate with our federal law enforcement partners”. But she acknowledged a shift had taken place after the 2026 midterm elections.
“The circumstances have now changed,” Dahlstrom wrote. “The election has concluded and the agreement no longer serves a continuing purpose.”
The reversal comes after months of pressure from the administration of President Donald Trump for states to surrender their voter rolls to federal authorities.
Trump has argued that such information was necessary to root out fraud during the November 3 midterms.
But officials in certain states argued that the federal government was encroaching on their constitutional authority. Under the US Constitution, only states have the power to administer elections.
Experts have also called Trump’s claims of “rigged” elections unsubstantiated.
No voters flagged for removal
The memorandum, signed last December at the Justice Department’s behest, established terms under which federal officials could flag potentially ineligible voters on Alaska’s voter rolls.
“Since that time, the DOJ has not identiﬁed any potentially ineligible voters or raised concerns regarding Alaska’s voter registration records,” the state Division of Elections said.
“No voters were removed from Alaska’s voter rolls as a result of the agreement.”
The announcement came as the state certified its November 3 midterm election results, in which Democrats flipped a Senate seat and won the governor’s office.
Alaska was one of several surprise battlegrounds during the midterms.
Democrat Mary Peltola unseated two-term Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan in a fiercely contested Senate race marred by allegations of a spoiler candidate recruited to sabotage the senator’s re-election bid.
Meanwhile, Democrat Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins won the state’s governorship, ending nearly three decades of Republican control in that office.
Democrats nationwide made significant gains, flipping both chambers of Congress in the midterms.
That result was largely fuelled by voter frustration under Trump, whose Republican Party suffered defeats in former strongholds like Texas.
A legal battle over voter rolls
Faced with drooping approval ratings in the lead-up to the election, Trump had falsely claimed that many non-citizens were registered to vote across the country.
His administration sued some 30 states as well as Washington, DC, after they declined to hand over their unredacted voter rolls for review.
Twenty-eight of those cases were ultimately dismissed in court, according to the Brennan Center for Justice, a public policy institute at New York University.
The Justice Department suffered a further setback last month when a federal judge struck down its nationwide voter-list maintenance programme, ruling that it lacked legal authority to collect and assess state registration lists. The administration has appealed the ruling.
Alaska was one of at least 16 states that complied with the administration’s demands for voter roll access.
But it was sued by voting rights advocates for surrendering voter information, in violation of the Alaska Constitution.
In its Monday statement, Alaska’s Division of Elections said it had directed the Justice Department to destroy Alaska’s confidential voter information in accordance with the 2025 memo — a move that could have implications for the pending lawsuit.
On Tuesday, Democratic State Senator Bill Wielechowski suggested the latest termination was timed to prevent further scrutiny from the lawsuit.
“The real reason they did this is to try to make the lawsuit over this release go away before the incoming Gov. Kreiss-Tomkins Administration could settle or produce discovery,” Wielechowski wrote on social media.
Kreiss-Tomkins is set to be sworn in as governor on December 7.
Wielechowski also noted that Alaska’s request for the Trump administration to delete the records is “likely meaningless”, since federal authorities have “undoubtedly already loaded it” onto government databases.
In its Monday statement, Alaska’s Division of Elections said its decision to end the memo did not constitute an admission of wrongdoing.
The state’s interests, it added, were “best served by terminating the agreement and continuing to rely on its established voter list-maintenance procedures”.
A Justice Department spokesperson told The Associated Press on Tuesday that the department would issue a formal response to the state.

items.title: Yale’s Sonnenfeld: Nvidia is a ‘detriment’ to U.S. industrial might — not a champion

items.text:
What the market celebrated Monday could prove to be a giant mistake, and not just for Nvidia’s board. Renowned business academic Jeffrey Sonnenfeld of Yale says the directors who reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO and also returned him to the board — even as the board says it is investigating whether foreign intelligence efforts targeted him — face a “historic level of individual liability.”
Nvidia’s chairman had effectively ruled out a reinstatement just last week. Then, in a torrent of private weekend calls led by Vice President JD Vance, top administration officials leaned on the board to bring Huang back, with President Trump calling the board directly to vouch for him. “I made the deal,” Trump told CNBC on Monday.
In an interview Tuesday morning, Sonnenfeld wondered whether the market is feting a company that’s largely responsible for putting sophisticated technology in the hands of the country’s adversaries, at a moment when the risks couldn’t be higher.
He pointed to research suggesting Nvidia’s most advanced chips have reached China despite U.S. export controls, and to sinking shares of Anthropic, which he links to the realization that China’s seemingly miraculous open-source AI models are in a sense copies of top U.S. labs’ work. Indeed, Huang’s return was greeted with relief in Asia, The Washington Post reported. “The king is back!” read one headline from China’s state-affiliated Star Market Daily.
The legal deluge has already begun. As we noted a couple of weeks ago, a potential class-action lawsuit was filed almost immediately. Days later, a shareholder derivative suit followed. Filed on Nvidia’s behalf against the directors themselves, the suit alleges the board ignored red flags about Huang’s relationship with suspected Chinese spy Alice Huang.
The class action is very much aimed at making Nvidia and Huang compensate investors for their losses, while the derivative suit puts the directors’ own behavior on trial, with any recovery going to Nvidia. Three more suits followed on Nov. 18, the day after Nvidia’s most recent earnings call; all five were filed in Northern California, where Nvidia is based.
Huang and Nvidia are also juggling a Justice Department antitrust investigation, a reported SEC probe into Nvidia’s accounting, a possible FBI review, a California subpoena, an export-control case that landed partner Megaspeed on the U.S. trade blacklist on Monday, and congressional inquiries, including a Senate Banking hearing next week at which Huang has agreed to testify.
Here’s some of what Sonnenfeld had to say, in a Q&A that’s been edited for length and clarity.
TC: So much has happened since we last talked. Huang was ousted, he’s come back. Do you think the board’s reliance on government assurances here is defensible or an abdication of its own duties?
JS: They failed to rely on experts. That’s one of the reasons this board is going to be sued and lose, and these directors are likely to face a historic level of individual liability. They have a very inadequate directors and officers liability policy. They have also just failed in their diligence. They hired the Wachtell [law] firm. The Wachtell firm barely got off the blocks to do an investigation. And then they have already reversed themselves, so they didn’t use the expertise needed.
It’s wild that they also put Huang right back on the board of directors.
The board showed, in addition to incompetence and collaboration, just cowardice in their capitulation because Trump has nothing to wave over them. If this was SpaceX, where 46% of its business comes from the government [you could maybe see the case for Trump’s involvement].For Nvidia, it’s not even 1% of its business that comes from the U.S. government, so [the board] didn’t have that threat. [Trump] can call off [federal] investigations, but he can’t call off the shareholder litigation. Some are already filed, and the estimates are there’ll probably be 30 of them, and they’re going to be extremely costly.
And this is not, by the way, just a blue or red state issue. We already have 14 GOP senators who’ve already come out against this, and very prominent conservatives, like Pete Ricketts and Josh Hawley and Tom Cotton and John Cornyn. Those are some issues that may help explain why Nvidia’s stock is tumbling today.
Might the board say, ‘We saw the classified intelligence findings, and they assure us Jensen will be absolved of wrongdoing’?
They haven’t seen those findings, and we also haven’t seen what will be the result of the Senate Intelligence Committee, the Senate Special Committee on Investigations, the Senate Banking Committee, and all their House counterparts. The board hasn’t seen any of that, and even if they saw it, which they have not yet, that still wouldn’t matter.
Do you think the Commerce Department will continue to tighten its chip export controls to keep China from accessing so much compute or walk back some of those recent moves?
We already see that Megaspeed has finally been put on the sanctions list, as it should have been before. And we have documentation now that Nvidia, rather than a champion of U.S. global industrial might, is actually a detriment to U.S. global industrial might, because their chips have now turned out to be in the hands and in the systems of not just the Chinese military, as they got channeled to Northwestern Polytechnical University, which is a military institution — this is going into weapons that will, of course, be funneled to Iran and Russia, and they didn’t have access to that a year ago. [Editor’s note: China has long denied supplying weapons to either country. Nvidia chips have been found in Russian drones, however, and the U.S. ambassador to China said in September that President Trump had discussed selling arms to China, an account Trump has denied.]

items.title: Bellingham plays down Zidane comparison after wonder goal
items.summary:
Bellingham plays down Zidane comparison after wonder goal
- Published
Manager Jose Mourinho described Jude Bellingham as "without any doubt, the best midfielder in the world" following a wonder goal which inspired a brilliant second-half performance for Real Madrid in a 5-1 win against PSV.
Mourinho
items.text:
Bellingham plays down Zidane comparison after wonder goal
- Published
Manager Jose Mourinho described Jude Bellingham as "without any doubt, the best midfielder in the world" following a wonder goal which inspired a brilliant second-half performance for Real Madrid in a 5-1 win against PSV.
Mourinho opted to leave the England midfielder out of the starting line-up for Tuesday's Champions League game at the Bernabeu - an understandable decision given the demands of Madrid's fixture schedule and the strength in depth at his disposal.
But after watching his side trail 1-0 at half-time against the Dutch side, Mourinho knew changes were needed.
On came Bellingham.
"He is an amazing player that has everything," the Portuguese manager said. "He has physicality, he understands the game, he has absolutely everything. Today, he has changed how the game was evolving."
Captain Fede Valverde equalised in the 50th minute and 10 minutes later Bellingham produced his moment of magic.
Receiving the ball just outside the penalty area, he took two touches to lift it into position before unleashing a magnificent volley with the outside of his right footr, leaving PSV keeper Matej Kovar with no chance.
It was a sensational finish, executed with extraordinary precision.
"I was a bit surprised, honestly," Bellingham said about the goal. "I knew that I could control the ball well and get it into my grasp. But normally from there, I'm looking to see who's on as an option to play through.
"It popped up nicely and I thought I'm just going to hit it. So yeah, it was a nice goal and important for the team, being the second goal, and gave us control."
The 23-year-old celebrated in trademark fashion, standing with his arms outstretched in front of the home supporters as thousands serenaded him with chants of 'Hey Jude'.
It was his fourth goal in his past five appearances for Real.
Asked whether he should be compared to Real and France legend Zinedine Zidane, who won the Ballon d'Or and World Cup in 1998, Bellingham maintained his humility.
"I think Zidane is much better than me. He's much more elegant and he's my idol," he said.
'I don't care about the Ballon d'Or'
Kylian Mbappe scored two more goals and Vinicius Junior put away the fifth to complete a super turnaround from a team that had looked short of ideas in the first half.
At the suggestion that he is currently in the form of his life, Bellingham said: "I think you're only as good as your next one [game]. Your last one doesn't really matter.
"But my focus has to change now to preparing for the next game. Thinking about my best form or being the best player in the world doesn't mean anything to me."
For Bellingham, the ability to respond when things are not going according to plan is what separates the best teams from the rest.
"We're managing to show that mentality that good teams do, that even if you're not playing well, you can raise the level at any point," he said.
His adaptation to life in Spain has also been an important part of that journey.
Asked about his increasingly impressive Spanish, Bellingham admitted he still gets nervous when speaking the language in public.
"It's getting a little bit better. I get a little bit nervous speaking to you guys. It's much easier in the changing room," he joked to journalists.
"I'm loving living in Spain. I'm loving the club. I think for English players it's such an important thing to go and move abroad and learn new things and I've obviously benefited massively from that."
And while his performances have inevitably brought renewed attention to individual awards, Bellingham said that personal recognition is not what motivates him.
Asked about the Ballon d'Or, he said his focus was only on the team.
"I don't care about the Ballon d'Or, honestly. I want to win a lot of titles with the team, the Champions League, the League."
"The Ballon d'Or is something for you, journalists, to vote and create a bit of tension. But for me it's more important that the team win."

items.text:
Kilmar Ábrego García is leaving the United States of his own volition, his lawyers confirmed on Tuesday.
Ábrego is leaving the US for Spain on Tuesday evening.
The Salvadorian immigrant was at the center of a months-long legal battle since he was deported to El Salvador in March 2025 by the Trump administration, in defiance of a court’s protection. He was held in Cecot, a notorious anti-terrorism mega-prison.
He was ultimately returned to the US following a decision by the supreme court three months later. Since then, Ábrego has been fighting a second deportation to a series of African countries proposed by Department of Homeland Security (DHS) officials.
The Washington Post reported earlier on Tuesday that he negotiated a deal with federal authorities to depart the US voluntarily in order to avoid being forcibly removed.
In a statement, the US senator Chris Van Hollen, who has advocated for Maryland resident Ábrego and who met with him in El Salvador last year, described him as a “free man” and referenced Ábrego’s agreement with the Trump administration.
“While the Trump Administration had been pursuing their vindictive prosecution against Kilmar and desperately trying to ship him against his will to countries known for human rights abuses, the Administration was forced to come to this agreement that respects Kilmar’s will and the due process rights guaranteed to him and to all in our nation,” Van Hollen said. “I am relieved that he will be safe, in a country of his choosing, and free – including from this Administration’s constant persecution.”
The 31-year-old has an American wife and child and has lived in Maryland for years, but he immigrated to the US illegally as a teenager. In 2019, an immigration judge ruled that he could not be deported to El Salvador because he faced danger there from a gang that had threatened his family. The judge allowed him to live and work in the US under Immigration and Customs Enforcement supervision, but he was not given residency status.
He was arrested in Baltimore in March 2025 and deported to a Salvadorian prison in what an official later called an “administrative error”. Facing public pressure and a court order, the Trump administration brought him back in June 2025, but only after securing an indictment charging him with human smuggling in Tennessee. A federal judge dismissed that case in May, finding that the justice department’s pursuit of criminal charges was designed to punish Ábrego García for challenging his deportation. The government is appealing.
The Trump administration vowed to deport him to a third country, threatening to send him to Uganda, Eswatini, Ghana and, most recently, Liberia.
“We will always admire his remarkable courage in staring down and defeating a vindictive prosecution instigated by the highest reaches of the Justice Department,” one of Ábrego García’s attorneys, Sean Hecker, said in a statement provided to the Washington Post. “He, in turn, is grateful to those who stood by him.”
The Associated Press contributed

items.summary:
Arteta says Arsenal need more luck to kill off games

In their past nine outings across all competitions, just once have the Gunners won a game
items.text:
Arteta says Arsenal need more luck to kill off games
- Published
It might be emerging more as a theme than as a major problem, but in recent weeks Arsenal cannot seem to finish off matches when they are on top.
In their past nine outings across all competitions, just once have the Gunners won a game by more than a single goal.
The latest frustration came in Tuesday's 1-1 draw with Borussia Dortmund, though perspective is needed. Arsenal might consider it as two points dropped having gone into half-time ahead, but they remain unbeaten in the current Champions League league phase and have not lost at this stage of the competition for more than two years.
But of late, despite dominating large parts of matches, Arsenal have had periods where they have dropped off and allowed opponents back into the game.
Against Slavia Prague away in the Champions League, after scoring twice in the first half, Arsenal's standards dropped. The same happened against Newcastle in the Premier League last weekend where they found themselves 2-1 behind in the second half having led at the break, before recovering to eventually draw 2-2.
They are producing periods of high-level football, but the struggles to consistently turn that into more goals can lead to nervy finishes.
In the draw with Bundesliga leaders Dortmund, Arsenal had 30 shots but just four of those attempts were on target.
Boss Mikel Arteta mentioned the failure to capitalise post match, though was keen to praise his side's "brilliant performance".
"The way we played, bearing in mind the opposition that we played today and what we've done out there, is just something to be very, very pleased [about] because there is very little more that you can demand from the team," Arteta said.
"But obviously, the feeling is that we should reward ourselves much more when you put that kind of performance in the amount of chances (and) situations.
"There is an element of luck; there is an element of us finishing the actions better. We need to insist because I think what the team has done and shown today, I think it's the right direction."
Missing chances or need more luck?
Arteta made six changes to the side that drew with Newcastle, with one of the biggest calls to rest striker Kai Havertz and bring in Viktor Gyokeres.
The striker has had a difficult season so far, with four of his seven starts coming in the Champions League against opposition where Arsenal have been favourites.
However, Gyokeres scored a powerful effort from outside the area to give Arsenal the lead against Dortmund.
Overall though, it ended up being a mixed night for the 28-year-old as he missed a header from inside the six-yard-box that would have surely won the game for the Gunners late on.
Arteta was asked if the chances his side are missing were down to mentality, misfortune or composure.
"Mentality, I don't know," he said.
"There is an element of luck here because how some of the goals they haven't gone inside, I don't know.
"The execution can be better, but everything that is in between that, I think it was really, really good."
Arteta was also full of praise for Gyokeres, with particular emphasis on the striker's link-up play; an element of his game at times criticised.
"What I love the most is how connected he was to the team," Arteta said.
"We used him many times in different ways. His link-up play, the way he held the ball, the way he threaded in behind and stretched the pitch.
"There was a lot to like in that performance and that's the Viktor that we needed."
City up next for the Gunners
Noni Madueke has been Arsenal's best attacker in recent weeks.
The winger, who was left out of the last England squad, is enjoying a run in the Arsenal starting XI with Bukayo Saka out injured and is taking his opportunity.
Madueke has registered a goal and two assists in his past three games and was again the best Arsenal forward against Dortmund.
The Gunners host Manchester City on Sunday and are currently six points clear at the top of the Premier League table.
Madueke, who was frustrated with the performance against Dortmund, said the clash with third-placed City is a great chance to get back to winning ways and shake off any frustration.
"I think these are the best games. I'm really looking forward to it. Two draws on the bounce now and I just desperately want to win on the weekend and I know my team-mates feel the same," Madueke told Amazon Prime.
"We are going to do everything we have to win the three points. We're champions, we're at home. We have a duty to perform well at the Emirates.
"There are things we need to improve but all in all we are going in the right direction."

items.summary:
Rebel group retreats in DR Congo after heavy clashes with government forces
CRP halts advance towards Bunia, citing commitments made during Ugandan-mediated talks with the government.
The rebel group led by convicted war criminal Thomas Lubanga has withdrawn from areas recently seized in the Democra
items.text:
Rebel group retreats in DR Congo after heavy clashes with government forces
CRP halts advance towards Bunia, citing commitments made during Ugandan-mediated talks with the government.
The rebel group led by convicted war criminal Thomas Lubanga has withdrawn from areas recently seized in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) after days of heavy fighting with government forces.
The Convention for the Popular Revolution (CRP) announced on Tuesday that it had decided to halt an advance towards the town of Bunia, the capital of Ituri province in northeast DRC.
In a statement, the group cited a commitment made in talks with the Congolese government, mediated by Uganda’s President Yoweri Museveni, as one of the reasons for its withdrawal.
The CRP’s decision came one day after the group seized the Iga-Barriere, a strategic area about 25km north of Bunia, forcing government troops to withdraw towards the provincial capital.
Lubanga, a former leader of the Union of Congolese Patriots, was convicted by the International Criminal Court (ICC) in 2012 on charges of recruiting and using child soldiers.
He was sentenced to 14 years in prison and released in March 2020 after completing his sentence. Lubanga remains sanctioned by the United Nations.
Lubanga announced the formation of the CRP in 2025, opening another front against the DRC’s President Felix Tshisekedi.
The group said the decision to withdraw troops was made “out of respect for the commitments made at the State House” by the Congolese government and the CRP, referring to an October 9 meeting hosted by Uganda between Lubanga and a delegation of senior government and military officials.
Disrupting Ebola response
On Sunday, the World ‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌Health Organization said fighting near a hospital in the Ituri province, north of Bunia, forced the evacuation of health workers and aid partners, disrupting Ebola response efforts.
The DRC is experiencing its largest and deadliest Ebola outbreak, which has spread across the country’s east and northeast. Ituri remains one of the most affected provinces.
Thousands of civilians have reportedly been displaced towards Bunia since the weekend due to renewed fighting between rebel fighters and government forces, according to local media reports.

New York jury convicts Huawei of stealing trade secrets
A New York jury has found Chinese telecom giant Huawei guilty of stealing trade secrets and other criminal offences, but acquitted it of a racketeering conspiracy and obstruction of justice. The verdict followed a three-month trial in New York
items.text:
New York jury convicts Huawei of stealing trade secrets
A New York jury has found Chinese telecom giant Huawei guilty of stealing trade secrets and other criminal offences, but acquitted it of a racketeering conspiracy and obstruction of justice. The verdict followed a three-month trial in New York in a case that adds to longstanding US efforts to curb Huawei's operations over alleged threats to national security.
A US jury convicted Chinese tech giant Huawei of stealing trade secrets Tuesday, but acquitted it of a more serious racketeering allegation, according to the Department of Justice.
The world's leading telecom equipment manufacturer, Huawei has been targeted by the Trump administration, which alleges a risk of it spying on behalf of the Chinese government.
The United States has previously urged countries not to use Huawei infrastructure for the rollout of new 5G mobile networks.
The verdict followed a three-month trial at a New York federal court, the US Department of Justice (DOJ) reported, with jurors finding Huawei guilty of 10 of the 12 criminal counts facing it -- including bank fraud, conspiracy to steal trade secrets and conspiracy to defraud the United States.
"No person or company is above the law," US Attorney General Todd Blanche said in a statement. "For decades, Huawei and three of its subsidiaries conducted their business in the United States on the basis of lies and theft."
The equipment manufacturer was accused of attempting to recruit employees of US telecoms firms and obtaining technological information from them in the process.
That data allegedly enabled Huawei to develop products similar to those of its competitors, which it then sold at lower prices, according to the original indictment.
"The misappropriated intellectual property included trade secret information and copyrighted works, such as source code and user manuals for internet routers, antenna technology, and robot testing technology," the DOJ said in a release.
Huawei even launched an internal program offering bonuses to employees who obtained industrial secrets from competitors, prosecutors claimed.
"Today's verdict sends an unmistakable message: America will defend its businesses, protect its workers, and safeguard its national security against corrupt foreign corporations that lie, cheat, and steal to get ahead," Assistant Attorney General Tysen A. Duva said in a statement.
The investigation also involved Huawei's business dealings with the government of Iran.
"Huawei repeatedly lied about the nature of its business in Iran, falsely telling banks, journalists, and the US government that it did not assist Iran's government, military, or intelligence community," DOJ said.
The jury ultimately acquitted the company of a racketeering conspiracy and obstruction of justice.
(FRANCE 24 with AFP)

South Africa convicts Zimbabwean who tried to fight Ukraine for Russia
The Zimbabwean man was arrested on November 8 at a Johannesburg airport while attempting to board a flight to Russia.
A South African court has convicted and sentenced a Zimbabwean man for trying to travel to Russia to fight in Ukraine after he was arrested earlier this month alongside eight others.
Tafadzwa Sithole was sentenced to five years in prison on Tuesday, under a five-year suspension, meaning he would only have to serve the time if he is convicted of a similar crime within that time period. Sithole is set to be deported back to Zimbabwe.
He told the court that he had agreed to fight for Russia in the war in exchange for “remuneration” after successfully applying online in Zimbabwe.
“He knew that the Russian Federation was engaged in an ongoing armed conflict with Ukraine and that the military service he intended to render would be performed in the context of that armed conflict,” his lawyer told the court.
Sithole was arrested at OR Tambo international airport on November 8 while attempting to board a flight to Russia.
Foreign Military Assistance Act
Sithole said a person he identified as “Albina” contacted him after he submitted the application, arranged accommodation in South Africa and provided a flight ticket to Russia. His admissions were detailed in a plea agreement with South African prosecutors.
He pleaded guilty to violating the Regulation of Foreign Military Assistance Act. The act prohibits mercenary activity and regulates military assistance to parties in foreign conflicts, including recruitment and training, and also applies to foreign nationals.
Sithole, who described himself as an unemployed third-year student at a university in Zimbabwe, appeared in court with four other accused who are also negotiating plea agreements with prosecutors.
He said he entered South Africa legally on November 4 and stayed in an accommodation in Kempton Park, east of Johannesburg, in preparation for his travel to Russia.
Larger issue at play
Zimbabwe is among several African countries where Russia has been recruiting fighters for its war against Ukraine. Others include South Africa, Kenya, Botswana and Ghana.
Zimbabwean authorities said in March that 15 citizens had been killed in the war in Ukraine and that they were seeking the return of 66 others. The government said recruits were promised well-paid jobs but had their travel documents confiscated and were forced into combat.
Kenya’s government said in February that more than 1,000 citizens had been recruited to fight for Russia. Families protested in Nairobi in March, demanding their relatives’ return and the prosecution of those responsible.
An investigation by Code for Africa, a nonprofit data journalism and technology organisation, identified 289 websites, domains and social media profiles used to lure recruits through false advertising and promises of generous benefits.

items.text:
'Pass, pass, slow, slow' - Man City's slick machine grinding to a halt
- Published
Manchester City's slick footballing machine is starting to grind to a halt.
The quick passing patterns and edge-of-the-seat action that was evident for so long under former manager Pep Guardiola was supposed to be taken forward by incumbent Enzo Maresca.
It started flawlessly under the Italian with the side winning their first eight games, but that smooth operation is beginning to turn into a turgid and pedestrian showing.
Similar to Saturday's 1-1 draw against Fulham, moans and groans filled a rather flat Etihad Stadium as the home faithful watched their side labour to a 2-2 Champions League draw against Napoli.
City's recent defensive issues also continued, now conceding in 10 successive games and letting in the first goal in seven of those matches.
Maresca said: "We are always looking for three points but when you are not able to win it is important you that don't lose. We take the point, five games [played],10 points and overall I think it is a good result in the end.
"Today, off the ball, once again we didn't concede a lot, the problem is that in this moment they are clinical when we concede a chance, almost every time it is finishing with a goal. We created many chances but in this moment it is like this and move on.
"The first 10 games we always scored first and then in this moment it is exactly in the opposite way, we just need to find a way to avoid that, but I don't think it affects the players in terms of their confidence. We fought until the end."
'Dull and predictable'
City were strong favourites for this game and should have had few issues in collecting all three points against a Napoli side that are languishing in eighth place in Serie A.
Their injury issues mean they were able to name only seven substitutes, two of those being goalkeepers, while they had suffered defeat in their past three meetings with City.
They threatened a shock result after twice going ahead through well-taken goals from Rasmus Hojlund and Noa Lang, but Rayan Cherki managed to salvage a late draw for the hosts.
Maresca's side had 62.7% possession and attempted 665 passes, which largely lacked incisiveness, and of that figure 303 were in the final third compared to Napoli's 77.
The latest disappointing result means City's perfect start is quickly unravelling, now having won only one of their past seven games in all competitions inside 90 minutes.
"It was really surprising to see Manchester City so dull in the first half and so predictable," former Scotland winger Pat Nevin said on BBC Radio 5 Live.
"If you play a team that takes their time, you get yourself set. It is 100% easier to defend.
"You sit and watch City pass, pass, pass, slow, slow. You can get a cigar out."
Is Haaland lacking service?
Star striker Erling Haaland has been in prolific form again this season, scoring 20 goals for club and country, but the 26-year-old has drawn a blank in his past two games.
The Norwegian had chances but failed to score against Fulham on Saturday and though he was handed the captain's armband against Napoli, Haaland was on the periphery for much of the game.
The frontman managed only 14 touches of the ball against the Serie A side on Tuesday, the lowest figure of any player that started the match.
It raises the question whether he is receiving the service to try and find the back of the net.
"I feel I am getting more than enough chances to score," Haaland told TNT Sports. "We tried to push at the end for a goal but we couldn't. Not good enough and we let them in too easy.
"Football is easy and difficult; when you win it's easy and you know what to do, when you don't you start questioning everything. The perfect thing would be to not think but it's not so easy."
City are sixth in the Champions League table, before Wednesday's games, but in the Premier League they have failed to win their past four.
It does not get any easier this weekend, facing a daunting trip to leaders Arsenal on Sunday as they aim to find some form.
Haaland added: "It's the most difficult game of the season going to the champions away.
"We need a top performance from every single player."

items.title: Champions League: Real Madrid thrash PSV 5-1 in comeback win as Manchester City held by Napoli
items.summary:
Champions League: Real Madrid thrash PSV 5-1 in comeback win as Manchester City held by Napoli
Real Madrid extended their winning run to 10 games in all competitions on Tuesday, overturning an early deficit to rout PSV Eindhoven 5-1 in the Champions League, with Jude Bellingham scoring a spectacular
items.text:
Champions League: Real Madrid thrash PSV 5-1 in comeback win as Manchester City held by Napoli
Real Madrid extended their winning run to 10 games in all competitions on Tuesday, overturning an early deficit to rout PSV Eindhoven 5-1 in the Champions League, with Jude Bellingham scoring a spectacular goal and Kylian Mbappé netting twice. Manchester City, meanwhile, twice came from behind to draw 2-2 with Napoli, while Arsenal were held to a 1-1 draw by Borussia Dortmund.
The Champions League followed a recent script for two of Europe’s heavyweight teams Tuesday, with Real Madrid — helped by a long-range stunner from Jude Bellingham and Kylian Mbappé's double — recovering to beat PSV Eindhoven 5-1 for a fifth straight victory in the league phase and City’s underwhelming form continuing with a 2-2 draw against Napoli in Kevin De Bruyne's latest homecoming.
Arsenal was held to a 1-1 draw by Borussia Dortmund and Como won again to move into third place after five rounds of games.
Slovan Bratislava, meanwhile, remained the only team on zero points after a 15th straight loss in the competition's main phase — this time 2-0 to Real Betis.
Bellingham's brilliance keeps Madrid on a roll
Make that 10 straight wins in all competitions for Madrid, whose resurgence under Jose Mourinho will be a concern for the rest of European soccer.
Things weren't going so well against PSV on Tuesday after a 32nd-minute penalty by Ivan Perisic for the Dutch league leaders.
Enter Bellingham, who had started on the bench and was introduced at halftime to revitalize Madrid’s attack at the Santiago Bernabeu Stadium.
After Federico Valverde equalized, Bellingham scored one of the best goals of this season's competition by teeing the ball up with the left foot, then with his right foot, before sending a looping volley with the outside of his right foot in off the post.
Mbappé added to the lead with goals in the 64th and 84th minutes, maintaining his record of scoring in every Champions League game so far this campaign, and Vinícius Júnior grabbed a fifth in the 87th.
Madrid, which previously had winners in the 90th minute or later against Roma and AEK Athens, has 15 points — three more than Paris Saint-Germain, which hosts Roma on Wednesday.
Cherki to the rescue but City in a funk
City's winless streak in Premier League reached four matches at the weekend, and there was no respite in the Champions League.
Rayan Cherki did at least rescue a point after City twice went behind to Napoli, for whom De Bruyne — a City great — started and was applauded off the field when substituted in the second half.
City looked in danger of falling to a second defeat in this season’s competition after Noa Lang’s volley put Napoli 2-1 ahead at Etihad Stadium.
Enzo Maresca’s team had already fought back from 1-0 down, with Ayyoub Bouaddi leveling after Rasmus Hojlund’s opener.
Cherki wriggled into the box and fired low inside the near post in the 86th
Two years unbeaten for Arsenal
In a clash of the English and German league leaders, Arsenal and Dortmund both scored high-quality goals.
Viktor Gyökeres sent a dipping shot up and over Dortmund’s tall goalkeeper Gregor Kobel in the 10th, before Maximilian Beier leveled in the 55th with a slick low shot past Kepa Arrizabalaga. That was created by a surging run from teenage French defender Joane Gadou.
Arsenal remains unbeaten for two full years in the Champions League main phase and next hosts table-topping Real Madrid in two weeks’ time.
Como on course for the knockouts
Como's debut campaign in the Champions League could hardly be going better.
There were none of the fireworks that marked the record 9-1 rout of Lens in the last round, but beating AEK 1-0 through Luis Milla’s rising strike means Cesc Fabregas’s team is surely heading into the knockout rounds
Como has 12 points and another win, maybe against Real Betis next, could even wind up securing a top-eight finish and automatic qualification to the last 16. After that, Como must play Barcelona and PSG.
Wins for Bodø/Glimt and Galatasaray
Bodø/Glimt and Galatasaray both left it late to earn scrappy 1-0 wins over LASK and Aston Villa, respectively, in the early kickoffs.
A humble club from a fishing town of around 55,000 people in northern Norway, Bodø/Glimt is making another run for the knockout stage — a year after providing one of the storylines of last season’s competition by advancing to the last 16, beating Man City, Atletico Madrid and Inter Milan along the way.
The team now has two wins from five matches and is on seven points after Andreas Helmersen’s back-post header deflected in off LASK substitute Melayro Bogarde in the second minute of stoppage time.
Villa was back in Istanbul for the first time since winning the Europa League there in May, beating Freiburg 3-0 in the final.
It wasn't an enjoyable return. The English club didn’t even have a shot on target against Galatasaray, with Deniz Gül scoring the only goal with a close-range header.
Feyenoord and Porto drew 0-0 and Lens lost a fourth game out of five, 3-1 at Leipzig.
(FRANCE 24 with AP)

items.title: Arsenal showing bluntless in attack - but Man City have problems too
items.summary:
Arsenal and Manchester City's problems analysed as both set to meet in bumper Premier League clash this weekend
Arsenal and Man City both slipped up in the Champions League in midweek ahead of their big Premier League meeting this weekend; watch Arsenal vs Man City live on Sky Sports Premier League

Arsenal and Manchester City's problems analysed as both set to meet in bumper Premier League clash this weekend
Arsenal and Man City both slipped up in the Champions League in midweek ahead of their big Premier League meeting this weekend; watch Arsenal vs Man City live on Sky Sports Premier League this Sunday, kick-off 4.30pm
Tuesday 24 November 2026 23:57, UK
Arsenal face Manchester City in a blockbuster Premier League contest this weekend, but in recent days and months, both teams have issues to overcome.
Arsenal have drawn back-to-back games against Newcastle and Borussia Dortmund, with Mikel Arteta's side throwing away comfortable half-time leads in both matches.
City, meanwhile, come into the game on a run of just one win in their last six Premier League and Champions League matches.

The game could have a huge impact on the Premier League title race, with Arsenal hoping to open up a nine-point lead over Enzo Maresca's side, who in turn could close the gap to the reigning champions to just three points with a win.
Sky Sports reporters Sam Blitz and Adam Bate were at Arsenal and City's draws in midweek and analyse their respective issues...
Arsenal showing bluntness in attack again
Sky Sports' Sam Blitz at the Emirates Stadium:
Arsenal have the most 1-0 wins out of any Premier League team since Mikel Arteta took over the club in December 2019. It's all well and good - until teams start making it 1-1.
And in the last two games, they have. And Arsenal only have themselves to blame.
After the Gunners' 1-1 draw with Borussia Dortmund, Arteta was convinced that their recent draws against Newcastle and the Bundesliga leaders are not comparable.
He claims Arsenal played well in this Champions League stalemate - and repeated on several occasions that Dortmund benefited from an "element of luck". There's an element of truth to that - the woodwork was struck three times in the second half.
But Arsenal had thirty shots against Dortmund - the most they've ever had in a Champions League game. Just four of those shots were on target. Seven shots came from within the six-yard box, no goals came from them.
And it's costing them points. Because there has been a pattern in Arsenal's last two matches. Dominate the first half, only take a 1-0 lead, start the second half slowly and then end up drawing the game.
Out of the 2.2 worth of Expected Goals Arsenal missed in the game, 0.96 of that tally came in the first half. From their 13 shots that didn't lead to a goal, they should have taken a bigger advantage.
It invited Dortmund back into the contest when there shouldn't have been one in the first place. Like Newcastle did at the weekend, the Bundesliga leaders sorted their game plan out in the half-time break and came out firing.
Arteta is right that the Newcastle and Dortmund games are different because Arsenal rallied to seize dominance of the game right after the German side's equaliser.
But once again, the conversation sits around the holes in Arsenal's attacking quality, particularly at left wing and up front. After Gabriel Martinelli and Gabriel Jesus left the club this summer without being replaced, Arsenal are still searching for attacking inspiration at left wing, with neither centre-forward in a goalscoring run of form.
Christos Tzolis is still waiting for his first Arsenal goal, Eberechi Eze is lacking consistency and Viktor Gyokeres backed up his early strike and impressive all-round display by creating doubts again by missing a late sitter.
At the start of the season, Gary Neville questioned whether Arsenal had the attacking player capable of delivering the Champions League. The draw to Dortmund backed that claim up.
Arteta struck a calm and positive tone after the Dortmund draw. It was a figure who knows his team have a six-point lead at the top of the Premier League, and will go on to qualify for the knockout stages of the Champions League.
But if these traits continue, it can all slip away quickly in this busy part of the season. If Arsenal don't beat Real Madrid, their top eight spot will be under threat.
Last season, they also benefited hugely from getting a top two spot that meant the second legs of their entire knockout stages were at the Emirates. PSG and Real can open up a bit of a gap on Arsenal in the coming weeks.
And up next, it's Manchester City at the Emirates. Enzo Maresca's side tend to score in most games. A 1-0 lead may not be enough.
Maresca still searching for the Man City solutions
Sky Sports' Adam Bate at the Etihad Stadium:
Move the ball quicker, yelled one fan from behind the press box. Press them, screamed a youngster in front. They were not wrong. Manchester City still have the individual quality to entertain the Etihad Stadium but they are also a frustrating watch at present.
City have picked up just one point from their last four Premier League games and while they did defeat RB Leipzig 3-2 in their previous Champions League outing, they let in two more in this draw with Napoli. It is 10 games now without keeping a clean sheet.
"Off the ball, the team was good from my point of view," said Enzo Maresca in the press conference afterwards, presenting a positive spin. "We did not concede a lot. The problem is that they were clinical. We created many chances." Not everyone agreed.
"It is not good enough," City captain Erling Haaland had told TNT Sports just before. "We let them in too easily and were unable to control or attack the game as we want." Tellingly, the striker then added: "When you do not win you start to question everything."
Maresca is being questioned. He has stressed that he is months into his time here not years and it is evident that he is still searching for the solutions. Finding the best role for new signings

items.title: Arsenal and Dortmund draw 1-1 as Gyokeres goes from hero to villain
items.summary:
Arsenal and Dortmund draw 1-1 as Gyokeres goes from hero to villain
Arsenal dominate the chances as Borussia Dortmund fight back for a 1-1 draw in football’s Champions League.
Arsenal striker Viktor Gyokeres showed why he is such a polarising figure with a thunderous goal and a crucial miss in Tuesd
items.text:
Arsenal and Dortmund draw 1-1 as Gyokeres goes from hero to villain
Arsenal dominate the chances as Borussia Dortmund fight back for a 1-1 draw in football’s Champions League.
Arsenal striker Viktor Gyokeres showed why he is such a polarising figure with a thunderous goal and a crucial miss in Tuesday’s 1-1 draw against Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League.
Gunners boss Mikel Arteta had urged Gyokeres to seize his opportunity after selecting the Swedish striker instead of Kai Havertz for the league phase tie at London’s Emirates Stadium.
Initially, Gyokeres looked like he was doing just that with his first goal at Emirates this season, and only his third for the Gunners in all competitions.
But the 28-year-old has been much maligned for his erratic displays since arriving from Sporting Lisbon in 2025.
And he gave more ammunition to his critics when he missed a golden opportunity to seal the points with a woeful header in the closing stages.
Dortmund had equalised through Maximilian Beier by then, and Arteta was left to rue his decision to put his faith in Gyokeres.
Arsenal are unbeaten in their last 11 games in all competitions, but this was not a vintage display by the English champions, who failed to win at home for the first time this season.
In a showdown between the current leaders of the Premier League and the Bundesliga, Arsenal were too profligate in attack and error-prone at the back to say they deserved all three points.
Arsenal sit fifth in the league phase with three wins and two draws from their five matches, while seventh-placed Dortmund are one point behind them.
Arteta will hope for a much more ruthless display in a significant Premier League showdown with spluttering title rivals Manchester City in north London on Sunday.
Arsenal were in control at the start, and Christos Tzolis’s strike bounced just over before Gyokeres tested Dortmund keeper Gregor Kobel with a long-range drive.
It was a warning Dortmund failed to heed as Gyokeres put Arsenal ahead in the 10th minute.
Fatally backing off when Gyokeres took possession 25 yards from goal, Dortmund’s defenders were punished by the Swede as he unleashed a superb dipping strike that flashed into the roof of the net.
Arsenal’s luck runs out in Champions League
Tzolis nearly doubled Arsenal’s lead with a curler that forced a sprawling save from Kobel.
Declan Rice almost replicated Gyokeres’s goal with a ferocious blast that fizzed just over.
Kepa Arrizabalaga was deputising for David Raya in goal for Arsenal after his fellow Spaniard suffered a shoulder injury in Saturday’s draw at Newcastle.
Such was Arsenal’s dominance that Kepa did not make a save until the final minute of the first half when he blocked Joane Gadou’s shot at the near post.
But Dortmund have a well-earned reputation as a stronger team in the second half this season, and they lived up to that tag once again.
Dortmund had a strong penalty appeal rejected after Gyokeres blocked a corner with his arm.
And with Arsenal unusually sloppy at the back, Dortmund’s pressure was rewarded in the 55th minute.
Gadou surged towards the Arsenal area before slipping a pass into Beier, who eluded Gabriel Magalhaes to plant a clinical low finish past Kepa.
Kobel saved Piero Hincapie’s close-range header as Arsenal tried to respond, while Dortmund midfielder Jobe Bellingham had a goal disallowed for a tight offside.
Gyokeres wasted his chance to finish as Arsenal’s hero for once when he sent a close-range diving header woefully wide from Martin Odegaard’s cross.
Arsenal’s luck was out after Odegaard’s delivery twice hit the post and appeared to strike Serhou Guirassy’s hand before it was finally scrambled clear.
Rice was equally unfortunate with a first-time drive that cannoned back off the near post to leave Arsenal frustrated.

items.title: Championship roundup: Boro edge Swansea, West Ham lose at Portsmouth
items.summary:
Will Lankshear was back among the goals as Middlesbrough cemented their position at the top of the Championship with a 2-1 win over Swansea.
Lankshear had missed the final two games before the international break because of a hamstring injury, and was only afforded a late substitute appearance in Sa
items.text:
Will Lankshear was back among the goals as Middlesbrough cemented their position at the top of the Championship with a 2-1 win over Swansea.
Lankshear had missed the final two games before the international break because of a hamstring injury, and was only afforded a late substitute appearance in Saturday’s win over Bristol City. Having been restored to the starting lineup at the Riverside, the Championship’s leading scorer claimed his 14th league goal of the season to re-establish his side’s lead in the second half after Joseph Opoku’s driven finish had cancelled out Myles Peart-Harris’ opener.
At the other end, Preston’s revival under Graham Alexander picked up more pace as they took Cardiff’s unbeaten home league record with a 4-0 triumph in the Welsh capital that moved them off the bottom of the Championship. It was their first win on the road this season and made it seven points from their last three games after a win over Southampton and a draw at West Ham.
Thierry Small scored in the 25th minute, Alfie Devine fired home in the 33rd, Andy Moran joined them on the scoresheet in the 62nd and then the captain Andrew Hughes headed home in the 69th. It was a tactical masterclass from Alexander’s men as they completely nullified Cardiff’s usual free-flowing approach and forced the home side into error after error.
Back at the top, Adam Armstrong’s double made it six goals in six games to give dominant Wolves a 3-0 win over Derby at Molineux that took them up to second. Armstrong’s double sandwiched Mateus Mané’s first of the season as Wolves’ fourth straight win stretched their unbeaten run to eight games to climb a place to second in the table. Despite a couple of first-half scares from Derby, Wolves could have had several more goals, while Derby are now bottom after one win in 13.
Scott Parker’s winless start to life as West Ham manager continued as Odin Bailey netted his first Portsmouth goal in a 1-0 victory at Fratton Park. Parker has lost two and drawn two since replacing Nuno Espírito Santo in the Hammers dugout, with the east Londoners without victory in six and 11 points off the top of the table. The Championship’s top scorers failed to scored for the first time this season, despite hitting the woodwork twice, as Bailey’s first-half strike was enough for Portsmouth to rise to 10th.
Sydie Peck equalised in the 90th minute as Sheffield United came from behind to secure a 1-1 Championship draw with Southampton at Bramall Lane. Lewis Dobbin had given the visitors an early lead but the Blades stepped up a gear after the break and finally found a way past the goalkeeper Daniel Peretz through Peck. The equaliser saw Sheffield United move within a point of the top eight and remain two behind their sixth-placed opponents.
Charlton swept Lincoln aside at the Valley with an impressive 4-0 victory. Joe Rankin-Costello’s first goal of the season quickly broke the deadlock with Ivan Mesik doubling the advantage inside the opening quarter of an hour. Tyreece Campbell’s finish early in the second half ended any lingering doubts that the Imps were heading for a fifth straight Championship loss. Miles Leaburn’s stoppage-time goal was nothing less than the utterly dominant home team deserved.
Bristol City stopped the rot at home by claiming a welcome point in a 1-1 draw with Wrexham. Michael Skubala, the home manager, had to endure chants about his employment prospects from the Ashton Gate faithful after Joe Worrall had given Wrexham a seventh-minute lead.
But City – who had lost their previous four home games – lifted mounting pressure on Skubala with a spirited display that took them up two places to 16th. Cameron Pring rewarded their endeavour with a rare goal after 51 minutes, the full-back on target for the first time since December 2023.
Norwich’s impressive run of victories came to an end as QPR held them to a 1-1 draw at Carrow Road. The Canaries had won their previous five Championship fixtures but had to come from behind to pick up a point this time around after Harvey Vale had fired the visitors in front just before the break.
Philippe Clement’s side were quickly back on level terms in the second half through a well-taken Anthony Musaba effort, but were well contained after that as Rangers registered a well-deserved point.

items.text:
Bellingham stunner, Mbappe brace help Real Madrid rout PSV
Real Madrid come from behind to power past PSV Eindhoven with a 5-1 win in football’s Champions League.
Jude Bellingham scored a sensational goal to help Real Madrid come from behind to thrash PSV 5-1 in the Champions League on Tuesday, continuing their 100 percent start.
Kylian Mbappe netted a brace with Federico Valverde and Vinicius Junior also on target for Los Blancos, who fought back strongly in the second half after Ivan Perisic sent the visitors ahead from the penalty spot.
Madrid climbed provisionally top of the league phase standings with their fifth victory from five European matches, and 10th consecutive triumph across all football competitions.
PSV put up an impressive fight in the first half, but Jose Mourinho’s side blew them away with a dynamic showing in the second, inspired by England midfielder Bellingham.
The former Birmingham and Borussia Dortmund star watched the first half from the bench, with Mourinho explaining he had a minor fitness issue.
However, with Madrid trailing to Perisic’s penalty, Mourinho called on Bellingham at the interval, and the 23-year-old inspired a memorable second-half display at the Santiago Bernabeu.
Ruben van Bommel drilled wide early on for Dutch champions PSV, while Vinicius crashed a shot off the bar at the other end.
PSV took the lead when Aurelien Tchouameni trod on Sven Mijnans’s foot, and Perisic rifled in the resulting penalty.
Mourinho made a triple change at half-time, including bringing on Bellingham, and Madrid were transformed.
Five minutes into the second half, the record 15-time champions were level, with Valverde finishing a slick team move.
Vinicius, who looked more like himself after a shaky start to the season, crossed for Yan Diomande to feed Arda Guler. The Turkish midfielder’s gentle back-heel flick set up Valverde to drive home at the near post.
Madrid were rampant, and after PSV goalkeeper Matej Kovar saved from Guler and Mbappe, Bellingham netted a marvellous second.
The midfielder collected a loose ball on the edge of the box, flicked it up and then sliced a stunning volley across the despairing Kovar and inside the post.
Vinicius was denied one-on-one before Mbappe netted Madrid’s third with a clinical finish after being set up by Guler.
Mbappe, who has scored in each of Madrid’s Champions League matches this season, rounded the goalkeeper to add a fourth.
Vinicius scored his first goal for Madrid since August to wrap things up after Bellingham lobbed a pass in behind PSV’s battered defence.
Mourinho jumped up in celebration after Vinicius prodded home, with the Portuguese coach hoping it will herald an overdue return to form for the Brazilian international.

items.text:
Scientists discover quasar formed 630 million years after the Big Bang
November 24, 2026
- ESA's Euclid telescope revealed the most distant known quasar, formed within 630 million years of the universe-forming Big Bang.
- That's considered a very early development in the 13.8 billion-year history of the cosmos, and it smashes previous records.
- The light carries valuable information about the early history of the universe.
Researchers at the European Space Agency on Tuesday announced the discovery of the most distant, and therefore oldest, quasar ever observed.
The discovery, made by a German astronomer and his team, was published in the journal Astronomy and Astrophysics.
A quasar refers to an extremely bright core of an active galaxy powered by gas falling into a supermassive black hole.
Quasars represent a brief phase in a galaxy's life, during which the nucleus can outshine the rest of the system.
"As enormous amounts of gas, dust and matter fall toward the black hole, they form a swirling accretion disk that heats up to extreme temperatures and radiates tremendous amounts of energy, outshining the entire rest of the galaxy by factors of hundreds or even thousands," said astronomer and study co-author Silvia Belladitta of the Max Planck Institute for Astronomy in Germany and the INAF Bologna Observatory of Astrophysics and Space Science in Italy.
"This makes quasars visible across billions of light-years, allowing us to observe them from the very early universe. Studying quasars helps astronomers understand how the first galaxies formed and evolved, and how the supermassive black holes at their hearts grew to such enormous sizes," Belladitta said.
More evidence that black holes were extremely massive very early on
The newly discovered object, formally known as J1504+6252, is nicknamed Dún Aonghas.
The red dot in the image below corresponds to seeing the universe as it was roughly 13.1 billion years ago — just 5% of its current age.
"I think it adds to the evidence that some objects in the early universe developed remarkably quickly. Just 630 million years after the Big Bang, this black hole had already grown to about 360 million times the mass of the sun and was shining as a quasar," said astronomer Julien Wolf of the European Southern Observatory in Germany, lead author of the research.
The discovery then supports the scenario in which supermassive black holes form through the direct collapse of large gas clouds and subsequently accumulate additional matter.
Dún Aonghas was first detected by the European Space Agency's Euclid telescope, with images having been characterized using a combination of ground- and space-based telescopes.
The ESA's orbiting telescope is meant for missions that uncover the mysteries of dark matter, which is the invisible glue lumping galaxies together, and dark energy, the force that pushes them apart.

items.title: Jensen Huang still thinks a succession plan creates unnecessary hierarchy

The topic of succession planning also came up — a p
items.text:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang kicked off his return to the chipmaker he co-founded by holding an all-hands meeting that covered remorse, therapy, and even the company’s code of conduct, according to accounts from multiple insiders who spoke to the media.
The topic of succession planning also came up — a particularly sticky issue seen as a key risk at Nvidia. Huang reportedly told staff that Nvidia doesn’t require succession planning because of its unique business model, CNBC reported, citing an unnamed source who was present. Surprisingly, given the events of the last two weeks, Huang argued that a succession plan would create unnecessary hierarchy.
Investors and analysts saw the issue differently earlier this month, when Huang resigned as CEO following his admission that he had extramarital affairs with at least two people, including one whom the U.S. government suspects of being a Chinese spy.
Nvidia is a flat organization, unlike other large corporations that have a swath of C-suite executives and multiple layers of management. Huang sits at the top and says he has about 60 direct reports. Nvidia has just five executive officers running the show, including Huang. The other four are CFO Colette Kress, who was interim CEO for 12 days; Ajay Puri, who heads worldwide field operations; Debora Shoquist, executive vice president of operations; and Timothy Teter, executive vice president and general counsel, according to the company’s regulatory filings.
Huang has previously defended the company’s structure in numerous interviews, including one in March with podcaster Lex Fridman.
“When you’re designing a company, you should first think about what is it that you want the company to produce,” Huang said in the interview. “You know, I see a lot of companies’ organization charts, and they all look the same. Hamburger [company] organization charts, software organization charts, and car company organization charts. They all look the same. And it doesn’t make any sense to me. You know, the goal of company is to be the machinery, the mechanism, the system that produces the output. And that output is the product that we like to create.”
Huang’s comments to staff, and his previous remarks on the topic of succession, may not be enough to assuage the board or shareholders over the long term, however.

items.title: Rayan Cherki magic denies Napoli but Manchester City’s struggles continue
items.summary: This was the perfect snapshot of Manchester City’s autumn difficulties.
