items.title: The U.S. government is investigating Iranian ties to as many as 50 hacked commercial vessels
items.summary:
The U.S. government is investigating Iranian ties to as many as 50 hacked commercial vessels
The U.S. government has intelligence suggesting that up to 50 commercial shipping vessels were recently compromised by cyberattacks, activity federal officials are investigating as potentially linked to Iran
items.text:
The U.S. government is investigating Iranian ties to as many as 50 hacked commercial vessels
The U.S. government has intelligence suggesting that up to 50 commercial shipping vessels were recently compromised by cyberattacks, activity federal officials are investigating as potentially linked to Iran.
That's according to a U.S. official familiar with the matter who was not authorized to speak on the record, a former military cyber operator and an industry executive briefed on the attacks. The series of breaches was first reported by the The Wall Street Journal.
The attacks against the maritime sector, if officials' suspicions are correct, may be the latest example of Iranian cyberattacks against global critical infrastructure during the ongoing war with the United States.
NPR has reported that cybersecurity experts and U.S. officials believe Iranian hackers were responsible for a series of digital attacks against U.S. water treatment systems across the country in August as well as a pattern of attacks targeting refrigeration cooling systems that led to spoiled food at grocery stores on U.S. military bases and all across Europe as recently as early November.
The Coast Guard and the FBI first partnered in August to send a "highly specialized team" to board two different foreign commercial vessels "in the Gulf of America" heading to U.S. ports, according to a statement provided by the FBI and the Coast Guard. "The captain, crew, and shore-side corporate staff were critical partners in helping to ensure the threats were mitigated," according to the statement.
The FBI and Coast Guard press offices also told NPR that there are no current "reports of operational disruptions, vessel instability, physical danger to crews, or environmental impacts."
However, there are dozens more ships in international waters that the U.S. government believes have been compromised by hackers and many others who might be vulnerable to similar attacks.
According to the U.S. official familiar with the investigation, bad actors took advantage of known vulnerabilities in Fortinet FortiGate devices, which are frequently used in the maritime industry. The Coast Guard and FBI released a cyber bulletin in September warning the industry that bad actors were breaking into these devices, which help manage firewalls and virtual private networks. "Threat actors routinely scan for specific, unpatched vulnerabilities to gain a foothold," the bulletin read.
According to the U.S. official, in some cases, employees aboard the ships suspected something nefarious was going on when they noticed email disruptions or couldn't log in to their accounts, or, in at least one case, an extended communications blackout. The U.S. official declined to comment on how the U.S. government knows about the extent of breaches across the sector.
However, according to the U.S. official, hackers were able to break in using the Fortinet vulnerability and then pivot from the ships' IT systems over to their network of devices controlling physical processes on the ships, what's called operational technology.
The U.S. official said the bad actors "could have impacted the systems on board that control propulsion, steering, navigation, and cargo management," though they did not share any examples of that kind of activity occurring. In at least one case, one of the ships affected was an LNG tanker designed to transport liquified natural gas. It's important to keep systems at a certain temperature to prevent dangerous accidents if a ship's cargo includes explosive materials –from chemicals to fuel.
While commercial vessels are accustomed to physical security reviews entering the United States following the Sept. 11 terrorist attacks, digital threats are becoming all the more important to track as adversaries can break in and cause damage from afar. "It's a totally new paradigm that these tankers are networked in this way," the U.S. official said.
Even so, national security officials have feared something like this might happen for years. A former Navy official who requested anonymity to discuss internal operations tells NPR that "we had been tracking the possibility to exploit and take control of [operational technology] systems on Navy ships and Merchant [Marine] ships for a long time, and now this is coming to fruition."
While the U.S. government is wary of advertising Iranian hacking efforts during the war, officials also want to spread awareness of the vulnerability of internet connected devices, particularly those that are linked to the technology that controls critical processes. "These are not sophisticated attacks," the official said. "This is a known vulnerability that could be mitigated with some pretty basic cyber hygiene."
"Modern ships are highly integrated systems. A cyberattack presents significant risks, including the potential for a collision, grounding, oil spill, or even an explosion. The Coast Guard regularly publishes bulletins on cyber vulnerabilities and actions vessel owners and operators can take to secure their networks," according to a statement from the Coast Guard.
Ahead of the winter and a busy holiday season for commercial shipping, officials are bracing themselves to investigate any ship entering U.S. ports that could be compromised.
"People never think about what a modern blessing electricity is until it goes out. People take the marine transportation system for granted until there's a problem and their stuff doesn't get there by Christmas," the U.S. official said. "I wish more Americans knew how complex this system is."

items.text:
Hostage situation reported in Colombia as armed men flee into supermarket
President Abelardo de la Espriella says police and military have been deployed as situation unfolds in Cartagena.
About 25 people are being held hostage at a supermarket in the Colombian city of Cartagena, where a group of armed men fled after an unsuccessful attempt to rob an armoured vehicle.
President Abelardo de la Espriella said on Tuesday that police and armed forces have been deployed to the scene.
He explained that the robbers sought refuge in a nearby store after security camera operators alerted police to the attempted robbery.
“Thirty people were kidnapped, five of whom have already been released. They are older women,” said de la Espriella. “All the capabilities of our various security forces have now been deployed, including special units.”
Images from the Reuters news agency showed heavily armed police and military personnel outside the Exito supermarket in the neighbourhood of La Castellana.
Unverified footage shared on social media appeared to show people inside the market kneeling against the windows with their hands bound.
The incident comes as de la Espriella, who campaigned on a promise to crack down on crime, faces a series of high-profile incidents that underscore the country’s ongoing issues with violence and insecurity.
The president made his remarks from the city of Villavicencio, where he had travelled in the aftermath of a recent car bombing the government has attributed to an armed group.
Already, politicians like former left-wing President Gustavo Petro have weighed in on the incident, blaming failures in de la Espriella’s security platform.
“The root cause of this violence is the impoverishment of the population, brought about by the collapse of the tourism sector,” Petro, de la Espriella’s predecessor, wrote on social media.
“Destroying tourism — through state-sanctioned violence, such as the desecration of corpses, and by making death the central theme of presidential discourse — has dismantled a dynamic source of wealth that once attracted 7 million foreign tourists.”
De la Espriella beat Petro’s handpicked successor, Senator Ivan Cepeda, in a June 21 run-off election.

In a two-month trial
items.text:
Huawei found guilty of stealing trade secrets but acquitted of racketeering
- Published
Huawei has been found guilty of conspiracy to steal trade secrets and bank fraud, but not guilty of the more serious overarching racketeering charge in a landmark trial in the US, AP reports.
In a two-month trial, prosecutors accused the Chinese technology and telecommunications giant of lying, cheating and stealing to gain any competitive advantage.
Huawei's defence team argued that prosecutors had decided Huawei was a criminal organisation and built its case from there, but the firm's success was due to its own innovation.
In a statement, Huawei said the racketeering acquittal "confirms that these allegations lack factual basis and vindicates our consistent position over the past eight years".
Federal prosecutors first announced the charges against Huawei in 2019.
During closing arguments last week, assistant US attorney Meredith Arfa told jurors Huawei spent 20 years doing whatever it took to expand its business, including lying to banks about its business dealings in Iran and stealing technology secrets from rival firms ensure it had a competitive edge.
However, defence attorney Brian Heberlig said Huawei had grown into business with operations in 170 countries and more than 200,000 staff through hard work.

The United Nations condemned as "abhorrent" the flogging of Iranian singer Parastoo Ahmadi and four members of her production team, urging Tehran to abolish the practice. The five received 74 lashes each on Monday following a performanc
items.text:
UN slams Iran after it flogs singer for performing without veil
The United Nations condemned as "abhorrent" the flogging of Iranian singer Parastoo Ahmadi and four members of her production team, urging Tehran to abolish the practice. The five received 74 lashes each on Monday following a performance viewed millions of times on YouTube, local media reported, citing Ahmadi's lawyer.
The United Nations branded the lashing of a prominent Iranian singer and her production team as "abhorrent" and said Tehran must eradicate flogging.
Parastoo Ahmadi and four members of her team were lashed 74 times each on Monday after a performance viewed millions of times on YouTube, according to local media reports citing her lawyer.
All the musicians wore black, with Ahmadi dressed in a long, strappy gown and wearing deep red lipstick, in a country where women are banned from singing in public. They are also required to dress modestly and wear the headscarf.
Read moreIran's courts order US to pay $290 billion in damages
Ahmadi, 29, was sentenced in June to the lashes alongside the others, for the concert posted online in December 2024.
"The flogging of Iranian singer Parastoo Ahmadi and four male members of her team – following a concert she gave without wearing headcover – is abhorrent," UN rights chief Volker Turk said on X.
"Flogging is a form of torture or other cruel, inhuman or degrading punishment, absolutely prohibited under international law in all circumstances.
"Iran must abstain from carrying out other flogging sentences and eradicate this practice from its laws."
Increasing numbers of Iranian women are appearing without hijab, especially since protests erupted following the death in custody of a woman named Mahsa Amini in September 2022. She had been arrested for allegedly violating the dress code.
(FRANCE 24 with AFP)

Eastern Libyan military commander Khalifa Haftar, flanked by his sons, arrived in Ankara on his first known v
items.text:
Libya’s Haftar visits Turkiye days after Ukraine hits Russian warship
Ahead of Erdogan’s Libya trip, Haftar’s visit suggests Turkiye seeks another way to bring the country’s rivals together.
Eastern Libyan military commander Khalifa Haftar, flanked by his sons, arrived in Ankara on his first known visit to Turkiye, just days after a long-range Ukrainian attack struck a Russian ship in Benghazi.
Arriving on Tuesday to the Turkish capital, the Libyan commander was greeted by Turkish Chief of General Staff General Selcuk Bayraktaroglu at the airport, according to photos released by the General Command of the Libyan National Army (LNA).
There was no official media readout of the meeting, but Reuters news agency reported that Haftar is set to meet with Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan.
Khaled and Belqasim Haftar accompanied their father to Ankara, according to the LNA’s General Command. Khaled is the LNA’s chief of staff, and Belqasim heads Libya’s Development and Reconstruction Fund.
Saddam Haftar, the LNA’s deputy commander and heir apparent, was in Doha for a separate meeting with Qatar’s minister of state for defence.
The visit came two days after Ukraine struck a Russian warship in Benghazi, the main city in Haftar-controlled eastern Libya, killing at least 10 Libyan and Russian crew members, according to local authorities.
The warship had docked to refuel and resupply under an agreement with the eastern authorities. Libya’s internationally recognised government in Tripoli condemned the attack on Monday, saying neither Russia nor Ukraine had the right to conduct military operations on Libyan territory or in its waters.
However, Turkish military support predates Ukraine’s long-range attack as Ankara helped the then-Tripoli government repel Haftar’s forces’ offensive in 2019 and 2020. Since a United Nations-brokered ceasefire ended major fighting in 2020, Turkiye has built ties with Haftar’s camp while maintaining its alliance with Tripoli.
On Saturday, Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan and intelligence chief Ibrahim Kalin met Abdul Hamid Dbeibah, prime minister of Libya’s Tripoli-based Government of National Unity, in Istanbul. Fidan later gave an interview to a Turkish television station, revealing Erdogan will visit Libya in December after a 15-year hiatus.
Ankara sets the tone
Khalifa Haftar’s visit to Ankara comes just weeks after Libya’s eastern-based House of Representatives approved a 2019 maritime deal with Turkiye, reversing years of opposition, largely seen as an overture towards Turkiye as power-sharing talks in the country stall.
Khalifa Haftar’s son Saddam Haftar is reportedly eyeing the Libyan presidency role, backed by Washington.
Championed by Massad Boulos, United States President Donald Trump’s senior adviser for Arab and African affairs, the US is currently trying to broker a power-sharing proposal between Tripoli and Benghazi that would make Saddam Haftar the chairman of the Tripoli-based Presidency Council (PC).
Powerful factions in Tripoli and the western city of Misrata oppose giving Saddam the post, Jalel Harchaoui, a Libya analyst, told Al Jazeera.
“The Turks are more pragmatic and realistic than Boulos,” Harchaoui said. Ankara takes that opposition seriously, he said, because trying to force the appointment could destabilise Libya.
As Haftar pushes for the president role, approving the 2019 memorandum of understanding signed between Turkiye and Libya’s UN-recognised former Government of National Accord (GNA) on the delimitation of maritime boundaries between the two countries in the Mediterranean Sea was an effort to secure Ankara’s backing for the council chairmanship position, Harchaoui said.
The European Union condemned the vote, as did Greece, Israel and Egypt.
Despite Saddam Haftar’s absence from the Ankara meeting, by inviting his father, Harchaoui said, Erdogan has given himself another way to show progress in bringing Libya’s rivals together.
As Erdogan gears up for a visit to Libya, the Turkish president may seek a meeting between Dbeibah and Khalifa Haftar as Ankara’s effort to carve “a format of its own, calibrated to its own risk appetite and independent of the one Boulos has been pushing for months”, according to the analyst.

items.summary:
US Army to detonate more than 4 tonnes of lead azide in Iowa on Wednesday
Despite alarm about toxic lead exposure, federal officials say destroying the unstable explosive compound is the safest course of action.
The United States Army has announced it plans to carry out two consecutive, rapid contro
items.text:
US Army to detonate more than 4 tonnes of lead azide in Iowa on Wednesday
Despite alarm about toxic lead exposure, federal officials say destroying the unstable explosive compound is the safest course of action.
The United States Army has announced it plans to carry out two consecutive, rapid controlled detonations of lead azide in the midwestern state of Iowa at 9am (15:00 GMT) on Wednesday, after a series of postponements.
The announcement on Tuesday comes as controversy continues to swirl around the planned detonation. The explosion risks sending particles of lead, a toxic metal, into surrounding communities.
But military experts warn that the lead azide, a compound used in munitions, will become increasingly unstable in the cold weather, risking an uncontrolled blast.
“Inaction is no longer an option,” Major General Eric Shirley, the army official in charge of the disposal effort, told reporters on Tuesday. “It would be irresponsible for us not to take the determined consensus-based course of action moving forward that has been selected.”
Shirley said the US Army has been working closely with state and federal officials.
The military has also taken a number of steps to mitigate harm to the public, he added. Earthworks had been constructed around the blast site, and cisterns were dug to collect any particles from the blast.
A political divide
The planned detonation has divided local political figures, with some questioning the safety of the military’s proposal and how the lead azide was allowed to reach such a state.
Others offered support to the US Army. Iowa’s Republican Governor Kim Reynolds, for instance, said the military was taking the right step in going ahead with the detonation.
“I believe, based on the information I’ve been given, that the danger is immediate, and I trust the Army will do everything in its power to protect the people who could be affected,” Reynolds wrote in a social media post on Tuesday.
The controlled detonation is slated to destroy 68 drums containing almost 4,500kg (10,000lb) of deteriorating lead azide — an explosive that has been used in military munitions since World War I.
The blasts are set to take place at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant, in the southeastern part of the state.
The facility is a sprawling 7,700-hectare (19,000-acre) installation near Middletown and Des Moines County, about 16 kilometres (10 miles) west of the Mississippi River, which separates Iowa and the state of Illinois.
Environmental groups have raised concerns that the planned explosions would release a cloud of toxic lead into the air, citing a government estimate that the plume could travel more than 160 kilometres (100 miles).
Those particles could eventually land on homes, crops and livestock far beyond the detonation site.
The Iowa Environmental Council and the state branch of the Sierra Club filed a lawsuit on November 19 to stop the detonation, and last week, a federal appeals court issued an administrative stay to pause the planned explosion.
On Monday, President Donald Trump also weighed in, announcing that he had also ordered the military to hold off.
He said that the controlled explosion could proceed only with the agreement of the federal appeals court and Iowa’s Democratic Governor-elect Rob Sand.
Later that day, the appeals court lifted its administrative stay, clearing the way for the US Army to proceed with the in-place detonation.
Sand has yet to weigh in on whether he supports the US Army’s plans. He has, however, advocated for greater transparency.
“Everyday Iowans are entitled to know how Middletown came to this situation, and learn why the administration believes this is the best path forward,” Sand said in a statement on Monday.
“That means they should have the same access to the information I’ve received in briefings from the administration, straight from the source.”
What happens after the detonations?
To curb potential lead exposure, federal agencies and the US Army have been rolling out guidance to nearby residents.
In a public safety advisory on Tuesday, the military instructed residents to turn off fans that pull in outside air and switch their heating, ventilation and air conditioning (HVAC) systems to a setting that blocks outdoor air intake.
The US Army also advised maximising indoor filtration after the explosion until the lead plume clears.
It is unclear the extent to which the US government will undertake cleanup efforts after the blast.
Under Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) policy, professional cleanup is necessary when as little as five micrograms are present per square foot (0.09 square metres) on floors, or when 40 micrograms are present on the same surface area for windowsills.
Those levels went into effect in January to better protect people — notably young children — from lead exposure.
Lead can cause developmental problems in children, including brain damage and speech problems, and among adults, it can also cause serious harm to internal organs, as well as during pregnancy.
Abatement efforts — designed to reduce lead exposure — are required only when the amount of lead dust meets or exceeds the action levels listed by the EPA.
But Bruce Lanphear, a paediatric epidemiologist and professor of health sciences at Simon Fraser University, takes issue with the use of regulatory thresholds as a measure of whether to act following the Iowa explosions.
Lead is already ubiquitous in the local environment, owing to decades of industrial activity, historical emissions and other sources, including the lead-based paint commonly used in the 20th century.
A post-detonation reading that falls below an EPA screening threshold would not, by itself, establish that little or no contamination has occurred, according to Lanphear.
“Cleanup should aim to restore lead concentrations to their pre-detonation levels, rather than merely reducing them below a regulatory screening level,” he explained.

items.text:
Introducing Ternary Bonsai 2.5 27B: Powering Agentic Coding and Private Knowledge Work
Today, we’re introducing Ternary Bonsai 2.5 27B, an upgrade to Ternary Bonsai 2 27B with substantially stronger agentic coding, multi-turn tool use, and multi-step task execution. Based on Qwen3.8 27B, it retains the previous release’s 5.9 GB model footprint while significantly improving the capabilities developers need to build agents that work with private files and tools on-device. The result is by far the strongest AI model of its memory footprint for agentic workloads.
With Ternary Bonsai 2 27B, we brought stronger reasoning, visual understanding, and tool use to local devices. Since then, we’ve focused on making the model more effective across long sequences of tool calls: interpreting results, adjusting when a step fails, and maintaining the task’s objective through the whole interaction. This release also continues our work to make Bonsai more practical by addressing excessive thinking and repetitive loops in the previous model. Compared with Ternary Bonsai 2, Ternary Bonsai 2.5 completes tasks in fewer turns, uses fewer tokens, and delivers results faster and more accurately.
Agentic workflows are particularly sensitive to model degradation: small errors can compound across successive tool calls and derail an entire task. Ternary Bonsai 2.5 significantly narrows the performance gap to the full-precision base model while retaining its compact footprint. Preserving this behavior through longer tasks is an important milestone in improving the intelligence density of models.
We evaluated Ternary Bonsai 2.5 27B against both Ternary Bonsai 2 27B and the full-precision Qwen 3.8 27B base model, as reported in the full whitepaper. We see marked improvements in agentic execution, coding, and multi-turn tool use, as shown in the table below.
On a single NVIDIA H100, Ternary Bonsai 2.5 27B achieves a generation speed of 291 tokens/s with MTP and processes a 2,000-token prompt at 3,200 tokens/s. Even on a consumer-grade RTX 4090, it delivers 204 tokens/s with MTP and a prompt processing speed of approximately 3,060 tokens/s. The demos below follow complete local workflows, from the initial request through intermediate decisions to the final result.
For products, this creates room to build assistance directly into the applications where work already happens: a coding assistant working through issues in a private repository, a document application that prepares reviewable summaries, or a desktop assistant that handles recurring analysis. Local deployment lets those products process sensitive material on the user’s device. Ternary Bonsai 2.5 27B strengthens the model capabilities behind that experience while keeping the compact footprint that makes it practical.
Platform Coverage
Ternary Bonsai 2.5 27B runs on NVIDIA and Intel GPUs via llama.cpp and on Apple devices (Mac, iPhone, iPad) via MLX.
Model weights are available today under the Apache 2.0 License.
Full technical details of our compression, evaluation, and benchmarking processes are available in our whitepaper.
Work with Us
We work with teams to tailor Bonsai models to their applications, from post-training on domain-specific data to optimizing inference for target hardware. If you’re building AI products with tight memory, latency, or power requirements, we’d love to explore how Bonsai can help. Reach out at sales@prismml.com.

items.text:
This was Aston Villa’s third trip to Istanbul in the calendar year but, this time, they departed with contrasting emotions. Unlike on the banks of the Bosphorus at Besiktas Park in May, scene of their unforgettable Europa League triumph, or at Fenerbahce in January, they came away with a bloody nose. Galatasaray’s matchwinner, Deniz Gul, came away with worse than that, needing treatment after taking a boot to the face from Nicolas Jackson as he scored from a corner on 77min, the game’s first effort on target.
Galatasaray maintained their commanding home form to extend Villa’s winless run to six in all competitions. A livid Unai Emery was booked for protesting to match officials as a low-quality game on a poor pitch ticked past five minutes of stoppage time.
History showed this was never going to be an easy hurdle for Villa. The Turkish champions have dropped points here once since the opening day of the season, a Champions League defeat against Barcelona last month. Galatasaray have now been beaten just once in 11 home meetings with Premier League opposition, with Arsenal, in 2014, the last English side to emerge victorious. Galatasaray beat Liverpool 1-0 here in last season’s round of 16 in March, before a comprehensive defeat at Anfield in the second leg. Eventually, in typically noisy, hostile surroundings, they overcame Villa by the same scoreline.
Villa had appeared generally comfortable despite the racket raining down from the stands. Taylor Harwood-Bellis looked strong on his first Champions League start. But Villa did not fashion their first opening – and first shot on goal – until a couple of minutes after going behind, the substitute Ibrahim Mbaye forcing Ugurcan Cakir into a save. While the assistant referee flagged the Senegal winger offside, replays suggested he may have been onside.
Emery insisted the pitch would not affect his team selection and so he made four changes from Saturday’s stalemate with Sunderland, his captain, John McGinn, returning to the XI together with Tyrone Mings, João Gomes and the fit-again Victor Lindelöf. Gomes was booked for a cynical foul on Yunus Akgun approaching the hour, a few minutes after McGinn was cautioned for a barge on Aleksei Batrakov, the 21-year-old Russia midfielder. A melee ensued close to the touchline but the referee, Daniel Siebert, was quick to defuse tensions.

Scotland supporters are permitted to let one ice-cold bead of sweat roll down their spinal cord.

Preamble
The champions and runaway leaders of the Premier League meet the leaders of the Bundesliga. That’s quite a sexy sell, even if it’s almost totally Jeopardy Lite™ (the official caveat of the Uefa Champions League Swiss System). Arsenal are on a roll, having won their last 12 group/league phase matches in a row; if they make it 13 tonight, they’ll equal an English record currently held by Liverpool. Throw in the fact that none of Arsenal’s 46 games against German teams have ended goalless, something that can also be said of BVB’s last 58 away matches in the Champions League, and we could be onto something here. items.title: Jensen Huang reportedly tells Nvidia staff it’s ‘not true’ Trump got him rehired
items.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang apologized to staff during his first all-hands since returning to the company, while attempting to distance himself from the narrative that the White House and tech leaders helped him get his job back, according to reports from Bloomberg, The New York Times, and The Handbaske
items.text:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang apologized to staff during his first all-hands since returning to the company, while attempting to distance himself from the narrative that the White House and tech leaders helped him get his job back, according to reports from Bloomberg, The New York Times, and The Handbasket’s Marisa Kabas.
Jensen Huang reportedly tells Nvidia staff it’s ‘not true’ Trump got him rehired
It’s also not because of ‘tech bro’ culture.
It’s also not because of ‘tech bro’ culture.
During the meeting, Huang reportedly called claims that President Donald Trump was directly involved in his reinstatement — an idea publicly promoted by Trump himself — “completely untrue.” He added, “Don’t think for a second politics played a role in the company. We are the most apolitical company,” according to Kabas.
Along with attempting to dismiss Trump’s involvement, Huang reportedly said he also didn’t return because he was a “tech bro” who was “above the law” or “above the code of conduct.” He added that, “no story has been more tortured than this one in human history,” Kabas reports. Instead, Huang said the Nvidia board “evaluated the entire situation,” while receiving assurance from the government that he posed no national security threat, according to the NYT.
Huang resigned as CEO of Nvidia on November 12th, following reports of affairs with an alleged Chinese spy and two employees, including vice president of healthcare Kimberly Powell. On Monday, Nvidia announced that it had reinstated Huang as CEO, president, and member of the board — a decision the White House said Trump was “totally involved in.” Trump also confirmed that he worked with Vice President JD Vance and other officials to bring Huang back. A swath of tech leaders, including Tesla CEO Elon Musk, Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney, and former White House AI czar David Sacks, were also in favor of Huang’s return.
In a post on Truth Social, Trump said that the government “has no reason to believe” Huang’s return poses a risk to national security, adding that the US attorney general “does not possess evidence” that he engaged in “unlawful conduct.” Nvidia is still facing an investigation over its accounting practices, according to Reuters. The company is also carrying out its own internal investigation surrounding reports that Huang was the target of a Chinese spy plot. Huang is set to testify before Congress on December 1st to answer questions about national security concerns, and Democrats are already planning to press Huang about his return, as well as Trump’s involvement.
Even after all this, Huang reportedly said he “doesn’t believe in succession planning.” He also acknowledged that he violated Nvidia’s code of conduct, adding that he is attending therapy daily, Bloomberg reports. “I made some terrible mistakes,” Huang said, according to the NYT. “I was unfaithful to Lori, and I hurt my kids and of course, I hurt all of you.”

items.text:
KISII, Kenya Nov 24- Kisii gubernatorial aspirant Kelvin Nyamari has defended his controversial distribution of women’s underwear bearing his photograph and a 2027 campaign message, following an uproar on social media.
Nyamari, who is seeking the Kisii gubernatorial seat, said the branding was intentional, explaining that he wanted to associate his campaign with the electorate, promote accountability and make his political bid memorable.
“I have been supporting girls and women through sanitary towel donations. This time, I decided to do something different by extending the support to include panties,” Nyamari said.
The aspirant found himself at the centre of an online storm after videos circulated on social media showing women receiving colourful panties bearing his photograph and the words ‘Governor Kisii County 2027’.
The underwear comes in different colours, including pink, white, red and brown. Nyamari’s photograph is printed on the front alongside his campaign branding as he positions himself to contest the Kisii gubernatorial seat in the 2027 General Election.
In one of the clips, a man distributing the garments is heard encouraging women to collect them and record the unusual giveaway.
The move has attracted sharp reactions online, with critics describing it as demeaning to women and a new low in early 2027 electioneering.
Some have questioned why a politician would choose women’s underwear as promotional material and print his photograph on an item considered personal and intimate.
However, Nyamari has remained unapologetic about the initiative.
“I am not ashamed of supporting women’s dignity and hygiene. Whether it is sanitary towels or panties, what matters is the impact we make in people’s lives,” he said.
“If my picture can help start a conversation about women’s dignity and hygiene, then let the conversation continue!”
“I would rather be remembered for doing something meaningful than for sitting back and criticising those who are trying to make a difference,” he added.
The controversy has not appeared to discourage the aspirant. In a subsequent social media update, Nyamari claimed that requests for the branded underwear were now coming in by the thousands, although he admitted that meeting the demand would be difficult due to budgetary constraints.
Nyamari is positioning himself to challenge incumbent Governor Simba Arati, who was elected in 2022 and is eligible to seek a second term in office.

Bayern hold 'constructive' talks over Musiala's health
- Published
Bayern Munich are only focused on getting Jamal Musiala back from injury and are not interested in the comments made regarding his contract, the club's sporting director Max Eberl insisted.
The 23-year-old collapsed twice in four days during pre-season and said he had been diagnosed with "easily treatable absence seizures, which are due to a neurological dysfunction".
Last week, players' union Fifpro said Bayern Munich's hierarchy "should know better" after the club's honorary president Uli Hoeness said the midfielder may never "regain the performance level he once had".
Describing the talks on Tuesday as "very, very constructive", Eberl said the focus was on Musiala's recovery from a recent injury.
"Today it was about just how we want to get Jamal back on the field, just like before his muscle injury in the international break," Eberl said.
"That's the only task FC Bayern has currently, to give Jamal this trust and not some topics about money or something."
The Bundesliga club's chief executive Jan-Christian Dreesen questioned the lucrative contract extension the Germany international signed in 2025, running until 2030, if Musiala fails to get back to his best form, while his predecessor Karl-Heinz Rummenigge suggested the deal, external may need to be renegotiated.
Bayern manager Vincent Kompany said in September it wouldn't be "a big deal" if the seizures return.
Musiala, previously a regular starter and one of the best young talents in Europe, has played five times this season, scoring twice.
"Contracts are there to be respected," Fifpro said on Saturday. "An injury or a dip in form gives a club no grounds to reopen terms it agreed to, just as a run of outstanding performances gives a player no automatic right to a pay rise."

items.summary:

Dan Sheehan has been suspended following a 'croc-roll' on Springbok loose forward Marco van Staden in the Nations Championship; he will miss Friday's fifth-place play-off against Aust
items.text:
Ireland captain Dan Sheehan to miss Nations Championship finale after two-game ban for red card against South Africa
Dan Sheehan has been suspended following a 'croc-roll' on Springbok loose forward Marco van Staden in the Nations Championship; he will miss Friday's fifth-place play-off against Australia
Tuesday 24 November 2026 20:00, UK
Ireland captain Dan Sheehan will miss Friday's Nations Championship fifth-place play-off against Australia after being handed a two-game ban for his red card against South Africa.
The forward was initially shown a yellow card by referee Christophe Ridley for a croc roll on Springbok replacement Marco van Staden in the 72nd minute of his country's 20-17 victory in Dublin.
The offence was subsequently upgraded to a red card by the foul play review officer.
- Ireland hold on for huge win over South Africa
- Nations Championship: Schedule, results for rugby's inaugural tournament
World Rugby law 9.20d states "a player may remove the jackler from the tackle area by pushing/driving them backwards (including by grabbing the knee/leg), but must not roll, pull or twist an opponent".
Sheehan faced a disciplinary hearing on Monday evening where the panel ruled the incident was a "low entry point" offence and merited a two-week suspension.
The 28-year-old has accepted the sanction and will also miss Leinster's United Rugby Championship meeting with the Ospreys on Friday, December 4.
Typically a hooker, Sheehan started at number eight for the first time at Test level against the world champions.
With Caelan Doris, Jack Conan and Sean Jansen all injured, head coach Andy Farrell now faces another reshuffle at the base of the scrum for the meeting with the Wallabies at Allianz Stadium, Twickenham.
Ronan Kelleher and Tom Stewart are set to continue as the two hookers in Ireland's matchday 23.

items.title: Turkish military helicopter crash kills five in western Turkiye
items.summary:
Turkish military helicopter crash kills five in western Turkiye
The Ministry of National Defence did not elaborate on the cause of the crash, days after another deadly army helicopter accident.
A Turkish Air Force helicopter has crashed in western Turkiye, killing five crew members, according to the
items.text:
Turkish military helicopter crash kills five in western Turkiye
The Ministry of National Defence did not elaborate on the cause of the crash, days after another deadly army helicopter accident.
A Turkish Air Force helicopter has crashed in western Turkiye, killing five crew members, according to the country’s Ministry of National Defence.
The accident occurred on Tuesday, 12 days after similar accident killed four people.
“An AS-532 helicopter belonging to our air force crashed after taking off from Eskisehir for training purposes,” the ministry said in a statement on Tuesday. “The wreckage of the helicopter has been reached and search and rescue operations are continuing.”
The ministry did not specify the cause of the crash. Eskisehir is home to the air force’s 1st Main Jet Base Command.
Media footage showed emergency teams at the scene of the crash near Yorukakcayir village, about 15km (nine miles) west of Eskisehir city centre.
The AS-532 Cougar is a twin-engine, French-made multi-purpose helicopter that is used by militaries across the world.
On November 12, an army Sikorsky S-70 crashed near Malatya in southern Turkiye, killing four crew members. No official explanation has been given since.
Turkiye has the second-largest army in NATO.

items.title: Luis Enrique insists PSG won't 'start crying' over Doué, Kvara injuries
items.summary:
Paris Saint-Germain boss Luis Enrique has insisted the club will cope with long-term injuries to key players Désiré Doué and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and will not look to the transfer market for January reinforcements.
PSG initially learned of Kvaratskhelia's injury after he ruptured his anterior cruci
items.text:
Paris Saint-Germain boss Luis Enrique has insisted the club will cope with long-term injuries to key players Désiré Doué and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and will not look to the transfer market for January reinforcements.
PSG initially learned of Kvaratskhelia's injury after he ruptured his anterior cruciate ligament in a victory over Barcelona last month and fellow influential attacker Doué suffered the same injury in their 3-2 win at Nice in Ligue 1 on Saturday.
The news serves as a blow for PSG who will be missing both star players for the rest of the season, but Luis Enrique ruled out replacing the pair in the January transfer window.
"We don't need to sign players in the transfer window, it's not our style to sign a player for just six months," he told a news conference ahead of Wednesday Champions League clash with AS Roma. "We're happy with our squad.
"Above all, we're not afraid of anything. We're confident in our abilities and our resilience. We're sad for the players who are injured, but our motivation is to share more great moments with them as the seasons progress."
Kvaratskhelia and Doué have been key parts of the PSG squad that has won back-to-back Champions League titles in the last two seasons, combining for 23 goals and 17 assists in those victorious European campaigns.
Doué added three goals and two assists in just three appearances in this season's competition before his injury.
Luis Enrique, though, is refusing to feel sorry for himself.
"Are we going to start crying and complaining? No, that's not how a team operates," he added.
"That's top level football. All the teams and all the coaches know that. Injuries happen.
"This team has shown all of its resilience over the last three years. We've always picked ourselves up. It's a challenge at the moment and we need to stay motivated to keep improving."
PSG's first challenge without their key duo comes as they welcome Roma to the Parc des Princes on Wednesday night.
The French side sit at the top of the league phase table and will be hoping to make it five wins out of five to strengthen their grip on a place in the last 16.
Luis Enrique, who was head coach at Roma in the 2011-12 season, said he is looking forward to the reunion.
"My time at Roma was very special to me," he said. "I have fond memories of it. It's a magnificent city; I had some wonderful experiences there as a manager, and I'm at peace with everything that happened to me whilst I was there.
"Clearly we're happy to be back in Champions League action, especially at home. This match will be very different from anything we've experienced before.
"They're a team that defends in a unique way, but we're looking forward to it."
Information from PA contributed to this report.

items.title: Champions League Power Rankings before MD5: Who's No. 1?
items.summary: We're officially past the midway point of the UEFA Champions League league phase as the 2026-27 European season rumbles on, and the grind of the calendar is beginning to take its toll on the elite teams, with injuries starting to pile up. Harry Kane (Bayern Munich), Désiré Doué (Paris Saint-Germain)
items.text:
We're officially past the midway point of the UEFA Champions League league phase as the 2026-27 European season rumbles on, and the grind of the calendar is beginning to take its toll on the elite teams, with injuries starting to pile up. Harry Kane (Bayern Munich), Désiré Doué (Paris Saint-Germain) and David Raya (Arsenal) were all sidelined this weekend with issues of varying severity, and it's only going to get more grueling as we head toward the hectic festive period and, beyond that, the January transfer window.
So what has it done to the standings? Throughout the competition, we will be asking our writers, editors and other experts to rank the top 10 teams in the tournament in terms of who they think are the strongest and most likely to win it all. Here are your Champions League Power Rankings going into a fun week.
UCL Power Rankings before Matchday 5
1. PARIS SAINT-GERMAIN (no change)
- Previous rank: 1
- Games since MD3: defeated Lyon 2-0; defeated Le Havre 5-1; defeated Villarreal 6-0; defeated Troyes 1-0; defeated Nice 3-2
- MD5 opponent: vs. AS Roma (Wednesday)
Would anyone bet against them winning it all a third straight time? Our voters were nearly unanimous -- 15 of 17 -- in crowning the French champions and back-to-back Champions League winners as the best team in this competition, but there are tough tests to come.
PSG continue to look sharp and ruthless domestically, which isn't normally their rhythm at this time of year. (Folks will remember that they generally wake up, form-wise, after Christmas, at least in recent seasons.) Ferran Torres keeps showing why he was such a savvy summer signing from Barcelona, chipping in eight goals and an assist as an occasional starter, with the likes of Senny Mayulu -- one of 12 players to get on the score sheet in Ligue 1 this season -- also stepping up to contribute in the attacking third.
They were managing without Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, who tore his ACL in October and faces a lengthy spell on the sideline, but Saturday's season-ending knee injury suffered by Doué in this weekend's win over Nice will tax their reserves over the course of a grueling campaign. Up next is a potentially tricky midweek date with Roma who, despite losing to Man United in Matchday 4, have one of the stingiest defenses in Serie A (11 goals conceded in 12 games).
2. BARCELONA (no change)
- Previous rank: 2
- Games since MD3: lost 2-1 vs. Real Madrid; defeated Alaves 6-1; defeated Aston Villa 3-0; defeated Atletico Madrid 2-1; defeated Villarreal 3-2
- MD5 opponent: at Sabah FK (Wednesday)
The Spanish champions continue to be box-office entertainment every week. They simply do not believe in drawing games; every single one of their games this season has ended with a decisive winner and loser, with their back-to-back losses to PSG and Real Madrid surrounded by wins up and down the schedule. Since the Clasico setback it has largely been business as usual, with big wins over Alaves and Villa followed by a very different pair of comeback victories at Atletico and home to Villarreal. Sunday's win had the feel of a predator toying with its prospective dinner, as Villarreal scored twice in the opening seven minutes to daze Lamine Yamal & Co. early, only for the champs to respond with three goals in 10 second-half minutes and a three-point lead at the top of LaLiga.
Like PSG, they have a simmering injury concern to their defensive corps, with several front-line defenders in various stages of rehab or treatment: Andreas Christensen has managed just 30 minutes of game time since mid-September, Pau Cubarsí's health is being monitored after a hip injury on international duty, and Jules Koundé/Eric García are just coming back from absences of their own. Rodri's ongoing fitness is a worry too as the best choice to shield a vulnerable back line, but as long as they are scoring goals by the bucketload -- their 51 in 13 LaLiga games is more than the bottom four teams in the table combined -- it feels like a minor concern. That said, Hansi Flick's side will need to tighten up once we get into the business end of this competition.
3. ARSENAL (no change)
- Previous rank: 3
- Games since MD3: defeated Everton 2-0; lost 5-3 on penalties vs. Fleetwood Town (Carabao Cup); defeated Liverpool 1-0; defeated Slavia Prague 2-1; defeated Hull 1-0; drew 2-2 vs. Newcastle
- MD5 opponent: vs. Borussia Dortmund (Tuesday)
The Gunners already have a six-point lead atop the Premier League after just 11 games, which feels like business as usual for Mikel Arteta's side, but the manner in which they slumped to a draw at Newcastle on Saturday shows that this side isn't quite at the juggernaut levels it achieved last season. Their aggressive press yielded the opening goal, when Kai Havertz snagged the ball from Lewis Hall and teed up Eberechi Eze, but Noni Madueke whiffed before halftime to double their lead and Arsenal crumbled after the break, conceding twice. Noni Madueke eventually atoned by rifling in the equalizer, but the loss of control and absence of ruthlessness will have Arsenal's rivals on notice.
This week's visit of Dortmund has all the hallmarks of a trap game, considering BVB are having a superb season so far and Arteta will have one eye on next weekend's visit of Man City to the Emirates instead. Shrugging off Saturday's torpor and asserting dominance over Niko Kovac & Co. on Tuesday will be essential to demoralizing the chasing pack.
4. REAL MADRID (up 2)
- Previous rank: 6
- Games since MD3: defeated Barcelona 2-1; defeated Racing Santander 3-0; defeated AEK Athens 3-2; defeated Valencia 3-0; defeated Celta Vigo 2-1
- MD5 opponent: vs. PSV Eindhoven (Tuesday)
Since Jose Mourinho announced his return to the Bernabeu this summer, we've been wondering when things would start to come apart at the seams. All the ingredients were present: a grouchy manager with a chip on his shoulder and no filter, a star-studded but temperamental squad in need of careful coaching, a demanding fanbase t

items.title: UAE Condemns Somalia’s ‘Hostile’ Approach, Accuses Mogadishu of Undermining Bilateral Ties
items.summary: NAIROBI, Kenya Nov 24 – The United Arab Emirates (UAE) has strongly condemned what it described as the Somali government’s escalatory and hostile approach towards the UAE, saying the actions reflect irresponsible positions that undermine bilateral relations and weaken the foundations of cooperation
items.text:
NAIROBI, Kenya Nov 24 – The United Arab Emirates (UAE) has strongly condemned what it described as the Somali government’s escalatory and hostile approach towards the UAE, saying the actions reflect irresponsible positions that undermine bilateral relations and weaken the foundations of cooperation between the two countries.
In a statement, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MoFA) stressed that decisions affecting relations between countries should be guided by shared interests and remain free from political considerations and internal conflicts.
The Ministry expressed regret over what it termed attempts by the Somali government to draw its internal power struggles into bilateral relations, warning that such actions could adversely affect the interests of the two brotherly peoples.
“The UAE closed its embassy in the Somali capital, Mogadishu, and withdrawn its diplomatic staff in January 2026, citing hostile actions by the Somali government targeting the UAE’s embassy and policies. These included decisions to cancel bilateral agreements previously concluded between the two countries,” the Ministry.
The Ministry of Foreign Affairs reaffirmed the UAE’s deep appreciation for the Somali people and its commitment to the longstanding bonds between the two nations, particularly those involving the Somali community residing in the UAE and Somali visitors.
“UAE remains committed to preserving and strengthening these ties and advancing the shared interests of the two peoples,” the Ministry reaffirmed.
Somalia expelled the UAE ambassador on November 19, 2026, giving him 72 hours to leave and recalling its own envoy from Abu Dhabi amid a deepening dispute over sovereignty, military bases, and regional ties.
Somalia’s President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud accused Abu Dhabi of bypassing th federal government to back regional administrations—specifically Somaliland, Puntland, and Jubaland—and of involvement in Israel’s recognition of Somaliland. Those three regions rejected Mogadishu’s authority to cancel deals affecting their territories.
Tensions center on port agreements in Berbera, Bosaso, and Kismayo and UAE military facilities in Berbera and Bosaso. Reports also note U.S. military activity tied to Bosaso and Berbera, while Ethiopia has deepened ties with the UAE.

Match report as Deniz Gul's strike beats Aston Villa in the Champions League league phase, with Galatasaray winning 1-0; the game lacked chances, with Villa failing to score for a second game in a row; Unai Emery's side have not won in six matches
Tuesday 24 November 2026 19:47, UK
Aston Villa's winless run extended to six games as a late Deniz Gul's header saw them beaten 1-0 by Galatasaray in the Champions League league phase.
It is the first time Villa have lost back-to-back league phase or group games under Unai Emery, putting them in a perilous position ahead of tough games against PSG and Borussia Dortmund in their next two European fixtures.
The Premier League side have not won since beating Manchester City on October 24, and have not scored since Leon Goretzka's strike against Manchester United on November 8.
- As it happened | Teams | Match stats
- Champions League fixtures and results | Table | Latest: Aston Villa
It was a game that lacked chances, and it took until the 79th minute - Gul's goal - for a shot on target. Villa failed to deal with a corner, with Nicolas Jackson's poor attempted clearance landing to the Galatasaray forward, who nodded home for his first Champions League goal.
He took a boot to the face from Jackson with the Villa forward attempting to clear. There was a VAR check for a possible red card, but nothing was given.
In contrast to Emery's side, Galatasaray extend their winning run to eight games in all competitions ahead of the Istanbul derby against Besiktas on Monday. They move up to 13th in the league phase table, and have now won three successive Champions League games - matching a club record.
Aston Villa remain in the top eight, but with the majority of the matchday five fixtures yet to be played. They play away to Ipswich next, live on Saturday Night Football.

23: OFFSIDE! Nicolas Jackson finds Johan Manzambi with a cute pass, which the latter fires straight at Cakur. However, the flag is up after.

52: CONFRONTATION! John McGinn and Aleksey Batrakov square up after the Villa captain barged the Galatasaray forward to the floor. It came after a reckless high challenge from Davinson Sanchez on Alysson.
64: CLOSE! Gul nods the ball back into the box after a great cross in, but Villa clear.
79: GOAL! Gul nods home after some poor defending from Villa, as VAR checks and clears a possible red card for Jackson.

items.summary:
Putin says retaliation ‘inevitable’ after Ukraine hit Russian oil plants
Ukrainian attacks subsided after Trump’s mid-October declaration of an energy ceasefire, but picked up again later that month.
Ukraine has continued its attacks on Russian oil refineries despite requests from US President Donal
items.text:
Putin says retaliation ‘inevitable’ after Ukraine hit Russian oil plants
Ukrainian attacks subsided after Trump’s mid-October declaration of an energy ceasefire, but picked up again later that month.
Ukraine has continued its attacks on Russian oil refineries despite requests from US President Donald Trump to withhold them, Russian President Vladimir Putin has said while threatening retaliation.
Putin made the threat on Tuesday, after Kyiv said it would stop striking Russian energy targets only when Moscow did the same.
Ukrainian attacks subsided after Trump’s mid-October declaration of an energy ceasefire in the conflict that began with Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. But they picked up again in late October.
“We see that the Kyiv regime continues to attack our refining facilities, despite the US president’s appeal and direct request to refrain from such attacks. But the Kyiv authorities are ignoring this advice,” Putin told a meeting of government officials and senior oil executives in the Kremlin.
“In this regard, I would like to stress that retaliatory measures on our part are inevitable.”
He also told the meeting that he wanted additional security measures for energy facilities.
According to estimates from two industry sources cited by the Reuters news agency, Ukrainian drone attacks have cut Russian oil refineries’ combined crude processing volumes by 45 percent since late October.
Several Russian regions have introduced restrictions on retail sales of petrol and diesel following a renewed spate of Ukrainian attacks on oil refineries, according to local media and authorities.
Putin said that while the situation on the domestic fuel market remained difficult, petrol prices have stabilised after they peaked in October.
Conflict widening?
Elsewhere, Poland on Tuesday accused Moscow of deliberately violating its airspace when a Russian surveillance drone briefly crossed the border.
Reporting from Kyiv, Al Jazeera’s Abdelaziz Mujahid said the incursion “may also signal that the conflict and these confrontations are widening”.
Moscow on Monday accused Estonia, a NATO and European Union member state, of a range of hostile actions “on the verge of triggering open war”, after Estonia announced the closure of their land border.
In other incidents, Warsaw said three Russian Kh-101 missiles landed in Poland on Friday, and a Russian cargo ship with links to the military was hit by drones and caught fire in the Baltic Sea on Saturday in an attack claimed by Ukraine.
On Sunday, Ukraine sank a Russian naval corvette in a Libyan port using maritime drones. Ukraine’s Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said the drone attack was a legitimate act of self-defence, following criticism from Libya’s internationally recognised government in Tripoli.
Additionally, British security officials on Tuesday warned United Kingdom companies providing “material support” for Ukrainian armed forces to brace for Russian sabotage attempts.
Civilian casualties
Meanwhile, a Russian attack killed two people in the Ukrainian city of Zaporizhzhia overnight, Governor Mykhailo Semikin said on Tuesday.
Forty people, including four children, were wounded in the assault, Semikin added. Images and a video on his Telegram account showed a damaged apartment building with its windows blown out and rubble on the ground.
The Interfax news agency, citing Russia’s Defence Ministry, said on Tuesday that the Russian military hit drone control sites, Starlink satellite terminals and other military assets in Ukraine’s Sumy region, also killing a number of servicemen.

items.text:
China Southern Airlines unit to buy 50 Boeing 737-8 planes
Boeing had not won a major order from China in almost a decade.
China Southern Airlines says its subsidiary, Xiamen Airlines, has signed an agreement with Boeing to buy 50 737-8 aircraft at a list price of about $7.4bn, according to a stock exchange filing.
The purchase agreement was filed with the stock exchange on Tuesday.
The actual purchase price would be lower than the list price as Boeing had offered Xiamen Airlines a “significant discount”, China Southern said in the filing. Large discounts are standard practice when airlines place sizeable orders with planemakers.
The order follows a commitment for 200 jets that China made during a summit between United States President Donald Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping in Beijing in May. The filing did not say whether this order is part of that commitment.
Boeing had not won a major order from China in almost a decade. Last year China reportedly prohibited its airlines from taking deliveries of Boeing jets. It also paused purchases of aircraft-related equipment and parts from US companies in the midst of a trade war, after Trump unleashed a barrage of tariffs on Beijing.
US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said in September that “there are about 140 [jetliner orders] that are in a good state”, with another 10 orders being finalised.
Trump said on Monday that he thinks China will buy another 250 Boeing airplanes. He gave no details, and Chinese officials have not confirmed any further purchases.
The planes in the Xiamen agreement are scheduled for delivery in batches between 2031 and 2034, China Southern said in the filing, adding that the deal is subject to approval from the company’s shareholders and relevant Chinese government authorities.
China Southern said the order would help Xiamen Airlines seize opportunities arising from its move to the new Xiamen Xiang’an international airport, support the construction of an aviation hub in Fujian province and optimise its fleet structure.
Xiamen Airlines, historically an all-Boeing operator, ended a nearly four-decade-long all-Boeing fleet in early 2023 when it took delivery of its first Airbus A321neo under an operating lease.
In April, China Southern and Xiamen Airlines also agreed to buy 137 Airbus A320neo family aircraft.

items.title: US House counsel denies backing controversial raid on Ilhan Omar’s home
items.summary:
US House counsel denies backing controversial raid on Ilhan Omar’s home
Legal counsel challenges Justice Department’s assertion of House’s involvement in controversial raid on Ilhan Omar’s home.
Washington, DC, United States – The US House’s general counsel has accused federal prosecutors of wrongly
items.text:
US House counsel denies backing controversial raid on Ilhan Omar’s home
Legal counsel challenges Justice Department’s assertion of House’s involvement in controversial raid on Ilhan Omar’s home.
Washington, DC, United States – The US House’s general counsel has accused federal prosecutors of wrongly claiming in court that the chamber’s legal office backed a raid on the home of Representative Ilhan Omar.
Court documents unsealed on Monday evening show that in the lead-up to the early morning October 12 raid on Omar’s home in Washington, DC, US Magistrate Judge Matthew Sharbaugh ordered the Department of Justice to give the lawmaker an opportunity to assert that some materials taken by them are constitutionally protected because she is a sitting member of Congress.
Matthew Berry, the House’s top lawyer, was tasked with helping protect that constitutional separation of powers for lawmakers, under a provision of the Constitution referred to as the Speech or Debate clause.
At court before the raid on Omar’s house, the Justice Department alleged it had consulted Berry and received his backing. Federal prosecutors told the court that Berry’s office “refused to be involved in the search” and that, “echoing the United States’ position, explained that, in his view, Speech or Debate clause protections do not extend to a member’s private residence”.
Berry told Al Jazeera that the Justice Department’s claim that his refusal to be involved in the search meant he agreed with the department was “categorically false”.
Berry acknowledged that his office had responded to a Justice Department email on the eve of the raid, saying that his office would not be present during the operation itself, but pointed out that a court had ruled Omar’s representatives must be given the chance to assert the constitutional privilege over which items were taken from her home.
“The Department of Justice’s assertion that I refused to be involved in the search of Representative Ilhan Omar’s residence because I agreed with the Department that Speech or Debate Clause protections do not extend to a Member’s private residence is categorically false,” Berry said in a statement.
According to court documents, Judge Sharbaugh rejected federal prosecutors’ assertions that the key constitutional provision shielding lawmakers from turning over work-related materials did not apply to Omar’s home, saying “this court sees differently.”
‘Unlawful search’
The raid on Omar’s home was widely condemned by Democratic lawmakers, who said it was a dangerous intrusion by President Donald Trump that violated constitutional separation of powers.
Omar’s lawyers, in a letter to the Justice Department after the raid in October, had said, “This search was neither justified nor lawful.” They said investigators did not provide them with a copy of the warrant in advance, and seized her phone and passport, along with other materials from her home.
Omar’s office did not respond to a request for comment from Al Jazeera.
A federal raid on a sitting member of Congress’ home was “extremely unusual”, and it would be highly doubtful the House Office of General Counsel would not want to be involved, said Timothy Heaphy, a former federal prosecutor who served as lead counsel for the House committee that investigated the January 6, 2021 attacks on the US Capitol.
The House general counsel’s office “represents the institutional prerogatives of the House. If a committee subpoenas something and there is an objection, the House’s General Counsel litigates that … if there is a Speech and Debate issue, they generally are involved,” Heaphy said.
“They would certainly want a voice in protecting the Speech and Debate privilege for members, regardless of politics. They are supposed to be bipartisan.”
The administration of US President Donald Trump is investigating Omar over alleged immigration fraud, with the president and top officials calling for her to lose her US citizenship and be deported.
Omar became a naturalised US citizen in 2000 after fleeing Somalia with her family as a child, according to her House biography. She has repeatedly rejected allegations by conservative critics about her immigration status, which was also probed in 2019 during Trump’s first administration.

items.summary:
Nigerian monarch, 92, suspended after sexual assault claims
- Published
One of Nigeria's best-known monarchs, the Emir of Daura, has been suspended from all official engagements and travel following allegations of sexual assault by a Polish tourist.
The visitor said Umar Farouk Umar, 92, had grabbed
items.text:
Nigerian monarch, 92, suspended after sexual assault claims
- Published
One of Nigeria's best-known monarchs, the Emir of Daura, has been suspended from all official engagements and travel following allegations of sexual assault by a Polish tourist.
The visitor said Umar Farouk Umar, 92, had grabbed her chest during a tourism encounter and that she felt disgusted by the experience.
The allegation sparked widespread discussion across social media platforms, with many calling for the suspension of the emir and an investigation - calls the Katsina state government has now heeded.
Umar has not commented on the allegations or his suspension.
He is one of several emirs - a traditional role dating back to pre-colonial times - who still wield great cultural and religious influence in northern Nigeria, although they have lost their political power.
Daura, where Umar serves as emir, holds an extremely important position for the Hausa people who dominate northern Nigeria. It is widely regarded as their spiritual homeland and the origin of the Hausa royal lineage, serving as the core of Hausa origin mythology and the legitimate foundation of traditional authority.
Politicians routinely visit his palace for royal prayers and to gain his support.
On her Instagram page, the tourist said she had spent 30 days travelling around Nigeria before visiting the Emir's palace on 14 November.
She posted a video, which has since been deleted, in which a man who appears to be the emir is holding her hands in his lap.
After some moments she was heard saying: "Stop, stop" as the hands reached for her chest.
According to a statement, Katsina Governor Dikko Umaru Radda directed the immediate constitution of a committee to investigate the allegations.
The statement said the state government was taking the allegations seriously and would rely on the committee's findings to determine the appropriate course of action.
It said the committee's findings and recommendations would be fully implemented, stressing that justice would be served.
However, it did not disclose the membership of the investigative committee, its terms of reference or the timeline for submitting its report.
The emir has been on the throne since 2007, succeeding his brother Bashar dan Umaru, who reigned for 41 years.

items.title: Life expectancy in Cuba falls for first time since 1950 amid economic crisis
items.summary:
Life expectancy has fallen for the first time in Cuba since 1950 as the island reels from a severe economic crisis, the head of the World Health Organization (WHO) said on Tuesday.
On a visit to Havana, WHO chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said life expectancy had fallen from 78.8 years in 2020 to 7
items.text:
Life expectancy has fallen for the first time in Cuba since 1950 as the island reels from a severe economic crisis, the head of the World Health Organization (WHO) said on Tuesday.
On a visit to Havana, WHO chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said life expectancy had fallen from 78.8 years in 2020 to 74.4 years in 2025, the first decline since records began in 1950.
The 2025 figures predate the US imposition of a crippling fuel blockade on the communist-run island in January.
The blockade, which builds on a six-decade US trade embargo, sharply accelerated the worst crisis in Cuba in decades, leaving state services on the brink of collapse.
At a press conference, Tedros painted a grim picture of a health system in “critical” condition.
He said the infant mortality rate had more than doubled, from approximately four deaths per 1,000 live births in 2020 to 9.9 in 2025.
Maternal mortality increased from 37.4 per 1,000 live births in 2019 to 44.1 last year.
Meanwhile, the survival rate for childhood cancer has decreased from 85% to 65% since January, when Washington threatened sanctions on any country supplying fuel to Cuba.
Tedros announced $2m in aid for childhood vaccination programs and the purchase of essential medical equipment.
He linked the health situation in Cuba to the “sanctions” but also referred to “internal problems” and said it was “positive” that Cuba was addressing them.
He was referring to Cuba’s announcement of wide-ranging market-led economic reforms.
“The reform the government is proposing concerns the economy, the market, health, almost every sector. And we support it,” Tedros said.

items.title: Israel’s Ben-Gvir accused of seeking ‘religious war’ over mosque raids
items.summary:
Israel’s Ben-Gvir accused of seeking ‘religious war’ over mosque raids
Israeli police have confiscated mosque loudspeakers as far-right lawmakers push legislation to restrict the call to prayer.
The recent confiscation of loudspeakers at two mosques in southern Israel is the latest example of an att
items.text:
Israel’s Ben-Gvir accused of seeking ‘religious war’ over mosque raids
Israeli police have confiscated mosque loudspeakers as far-right lawmakers push legislation to restrict the call to prayer.
The recent confiscation of loudspeakers at two mosques in southern Israel is the latest example of an attempt by National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir to “ignite a religious war”, parliamentarian Ahmad Tibi has told Al Jazeera.
Tibi said that Ben-Gvir, who oversees Israel’s police, was “exploiting the atmosphere of war” after he ordered the removal of the loudspeakers, which are used to broadcast the Islamic call to prayer.
Israeli police disconnected the speakers at a mosque in the Bedouin town of Hura and removed its sound equipment on Sunday.
Days earlier, police had seized the sound system at al-Dawa Mosque in nearby Tel al-Saba, known in Hebrew as Tel Sheva. Police said they had received repeated noise complaints about both mosques.
Ben-Gvir, a far-right figure known for making anti-Palestinian and anti-Arab statements and celebrating harsh treatment inflicted on Palestinian prisoners, defended the removals, saying that noise levels had been too high.
Tibi, a leader of the Ta’al Party – a member of the Joint List – accused caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of leading a campaign of incitement against Palestinian citizens of Israel. Netanyahu has attempted to delegitimise any attempt by the opposition to form a government with the backing of Arab-led parties, accusing the latter of supporting “terrorism”.
Critics – including Palestinian citizens of Israel and Israeli opposition leaders – have linked the comments by Netanyahu and other right-wing politicians, as well as their policies, to recent attacks targeting a mosque and an Arab city in Israel.
Repeated seizures
Ibrahim al-Asam, a Tel al-Saba resident and activist, disputed the police account, writing on social media that the speaker at al-Dawa Mosque was not loud. He said officers damaged the mosque during the raid and took the recorder connected to its security cameras.
Police said they had issued fines and warned those responsible for the sound system at Tel al-Saba before seizing it. In Hura, they said officers checked the volume at the mosque and found it exceeded the legal limit.
“The mosque is far away and doesn’t bother anyone,” said Atiya al-Asam, who heads the regional council representing Bedouin villages in al-Naqab (Negev) that Israel does not recognise. He called the seizure “an assault on people’s faith, on Islam and Muslims”, and said that police had acted without a court order, calling for the speakers to be returned.
The seizures are a continuation of an ongoing policy.
Israeli authorities took loudspeakers from a mosque in the al-Naqab village of Bir al-Hammam in April and from another in Majd al-Krum, in the northern Galilee region, in June. Authorities also summoned several muezzins – who give the call to prayer – for questioning and had warned mosques they could face fines.
The Palestinian monitoring group Mo’ta recorded at least 38 cases in 2026 in which Israeli authorities invoked noise regulations against mosques, imams, or muezzins in Arab and mixed Arab-Jewish communities in Israel.
But they are also taking place in the occupied West Bank. For example, in December 2025, the Israeli military ordered mosques in Ras Tira, near Qalqilya, to lower the volume of the call to prayer. The army distributed notices saying the sound disturbed nearby illegal Israeli settlements.
Mo’ta has reported attacks on 50 mosques in the occupied West Bank, including 13 cases of arson. In Hebron, the Palestinian Ministry of Endowments and Religious Affairs said Israeli authorities had prevented the call to prayer at the Ibrahimi Mosque 1,009 times since the start of 2026.
On July 1, Israel’s parliament, the Knesset, voted 50 to 36 in a preliminary reading for a bill that would prohibit mosques from using loudspeakers to broadcast the call to prayer without government permission. The legislation, sponsored by Zvika Fogel of Ben-Gvir’s far-right Jewish Power party, did not become law.
Jewish Power said on Monday that it would bring a new version of the bill for a parliamentary vote on Wednesday.

items.title: Florian Wirtz hails Iraola and Klopp as he reaches new levels for Liverpool
items.summary:
Florian Wirtz has credited Andoni Iraola with helping him recapture the form that made him one of the most coveted players in Europe when he joined Liverpool in a deal worth up to £116m in 2025.
The Germany international believes he is in the best form of his Liverpool career, having had a difficult
items.text:
Florian Wirtz has credited Andoni Iraola with helping him recapture the form that made him one of the most coveted players in Europe when he joined Liverpool in a deal worth up to £116m in 2025.
The Germany international believes he is in the best form of his Liverpool career, having had a difficult debut season under Arne Slot and also struggled in the early weeks of Iraola’s reign. Wirtz scored an exquisite improvised goal in the 4-0 defeat of Manchester United on Sunday when he also created 10 chances from open play.
Speaking in the buildup to Liverpool’s Champions League game against Club Brugge on Wednesday, Wirtz attributed his improvement to becoming “a bit better on a physical level” and gaining a better understanding of English football and the Premier League. The 23-year-old claimed he is back to the heights he reached with Bayer Leverkusen, when Liverpool, Real Madrid and Manchester City all challenged for his services, thanks to working with Iraola.
“I am really enjoying playing under him, he is a really good coach,” said Wirtz in Belgium. “He is bringing me back into the place where I was maybe two years ago where I played really good football. I can feel that he gives me confidence and I am really happy about that. I am just trying to give him back what he gives me.”
Wirtz has scored five goals in his last four games for club and country, also flourishing on international duty with Jürgen Klopp’s Germany. He said the former Liverpool manager has given him advice on how to prove his worth at Anfield.
The playmaker added: “We speak always about Liverpool when we have the time to do so. He had a great time here. He just tells me all the time that he loved his time here, the people love him here, he tries to give me some advice to be successful here because he has shown how it is done. It is small things, more private things. He is just speaking good about the club, the region, the people, and that helps to hear someone who has experienced it.”
Wirtz claimed his fierce self-belief has enabled him to handle criticism since the big-money move from Leverkusen. “It’s mainly a thing that goes on in my own head,” he explained. “It’s not about the people who talk about me. It’s the goals I set myself and the performances I want to show for myself. I always believed in myself. I knew my qualities, and I know them now.
“Sometimes there are phases where you have to work even more to get the output, but I’m just enjoying the moment and really happy that it’s going well. Of course there were days where I wasn’t happy with myself. I always try to work on myself and get better every day but I still believe it makes no sense to put too much pressure on yourself as that doesn’t help in the process to get to where you want. I just believed in myself so I wasn’t too annoyed.”
Liverpool will again be without the injured Cody Gakpo and Ryan Gravenberch against Club Brugge, who are second in the Belgian Pro League and won 4-3 at Inter, the Italian champions, last month.
Iraola said: “Sometimes you have to analyse a team and watch a lot of games and it’s a little boring but with Brugge that definitely doesn’t happen. They are a very attractive team. They are very energetic. Everyone runs and they are very aggressive in the press. They are coming in on an incredible run of games – 10 wins and a draw in their last 11. We will have to be at a very good level otherwise, it is going to be very difficult.”
